## Goal

Explain and, if it is a defect, fix the single `available_times` gate bypass observed while verifying LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO, so paid opencode spend can never happen inside the UTC gap windows (01:00-04:00, 06:00-10:00).

Discovered from: LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO (verification of LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX — off-peak low-priority fallback).

## Observation

In the post-change 24 h window (2026-10-20 14:44:27 - 2026-10-21 14:44:27 local = 13:44 - 13:44 UTC) there was exactly **one** low-priority fallback to an opencode entry inside a forbidden gap window, at **2026-10-21 01:00:05 UTC** (`log` 02:00:05 local):

```
2026-10-21 02:00:05,162 Skipping provider=opencode-go-2: outside its available_times window (UTC)
2026-10-21 02:00:05,162 Skipping provider=opencode-go: quota_exhausted (account=OPENCODE_API_KEY, ...)
2026-10-21 02:00:05,162 Fallback triggered ... from=munitoai-free, to=opencode-go-3, reason=rate_limited
2026-10-21 02:00:05,163 Stream started: provider=OpenCode Go 3 ... entry=opencode-go-3
```

Two seconds earlier (01:00:03 UTC) the same chain correctly logged `Skipping provider=opencode-go-3: outside its available_times window (UTC)` for another request, so the gate is not simply disabled for `-3`. Note that `opencode-go-3`'s skip line is **absent** in the 01:00:05 sequence — the third entry was reached already having "passed" eligibility.

Impact: 2 dispatches / 52,329 tokens (0.006% of the window's 828.5M logged tokens) — small, but the gap-window invariant is supposed to be absolute.

## Hypothesis (needs confirmation)

`_select_provider`-style loops call `_provider_in_allowed_window(provider_cfg, config)` with no explicit `now_utc`, so the gate reads the clock at evaluation time; but the request appears to have been in flight/across the 01:00 UTC boundary. Alternatively one path (e.g. the pre-existing in-flight/retry path or the 429-failover sibling hop) re-enters the chain without re-running the `available_times` gate — the surge-bypass helper `_provider_in_allowed_window` could also have reported True during a window edge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Root cause identified and documented on this item with a log-derived reproduction (specific code path, and why `opencode-go-3`'s skip line was absent).
- AC2: A regression test covers the identified path and fails before the fix.
- AC3: If it is a defect, the fix guarantees no opencode dispatch outside `available_times` unless the documented final-week quota-surge bypass (LP-0MVF7KJN2000ASE8) applies to that account.
- AC4: A post-fix verification statement records zero gap-window opencode dispatches over a full cheap window.
data.title: Investigate available_times gate bypass for opencode-go-3 at 01:00:05 UTC (2 dispatches in gap window)

data.description:
## Problem statement

Between the 24 h window anchored on 2026-10-18/19 and the window anchored on 2026-10-20/21, logged (paid-serving) token volume rose **+96%** (421.7 M → 828.5 M) while requests *fell* 29% (12,810 → 9,137) — i.e. ≈32.9 k → ≈90.7 k tokens per request (≈2.8×). Nothing owns that trend: the verification item that surfaced it (LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO) could only show the off-peak low-priority fallback epic did **not** cause it. Until the growth is attributed, we cannot tell an intended context-growth change from a context-budget/compaction regression or a token-accounting artefact, and we have no standing metric that would have flagged it.

## Users

- **Producer / cost owner** — needs to know whether paid-serving spend doubled for a legitimate reason (bigger sessions) or because of a regression, and needs the answer recorded where the verification record lives.
- **Proxy maintainer** — needs any regression found here either fixed with a regression test or filed as a blocking child with numbers attached, and needs the failing mechanism named (compaction, context budget, token accounting).
- **Operator reading the daily proxy-usage report** — needs a durable per-request cost signal so the next drift is visible on the day it happens instead of via an ad-hoc before/after comparison.

Example user stories:

- As the cost owner, I want the +96% rise attributed to a named cause with numbers, so I can decide whether the paid tier is behaving as designed.
- As a proxy maintainer, I want a `provider_context_exceeded`/accounting check that distinguishes re-attribution from real extra tokens, so I do not chase a phantom regression.
- As the report operator, I want tokens-per-request on the daily report, so a 2.8× shift is caught automatically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The candidate causes (genuine context growth, context-budget/compaction regression, token-accounting artefact, serving-tier mix) are each ruled in or out with a quantified two-window comparison — `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages` and `duration_seconds` distributions from `standard_sessions.csv` / `low_priority_sessions.csv`, plus per-serving-entry token triples (`tokens=prompt/completion/total`) and per-dispatch `routing_check ... estimated_tokens` distributions.
- AC2: The tokens-per-request increase is attributed to a named cause with supporting numbers, or explicitly recorded as unexplained with the residual quantified (e.g. "X% of the +407 M explained by context growth, Y M unattributed").
- AC3: Any regression found is either fixed here with a regression test, or filed as a child work item with the blocking relationship recorded (`wl dep add`/comment `Blocks:` / `Blocked-by:`).
- AC4: A durable cost metric is implemented (preferred) or, if deferred, proposed as a concrete child item: tokens-per-request (and per-session token totals) surfaced in the daily proxy-usage report with the trend visible across days.
- AC5: Findings are commented on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO so the verification record carries the resolution.
- AC6 (testing/validation): Any metric or parser change ships with meaningful tests (aggregation unit tests over fixture sessions plus an `analyze_proxy_usage.py` end-to-end assertion), and every number quoted in the findings is reproducible from a committed command.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, and `proxy/docs/routing.md` if a routing/budget mechanism is implicated).
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Log retention.** Both windows are still resolvable from rotated logs in `/var/log/llama-proxy` (verified 2026-10-22: `proxy.log-2026-10-18_00.gz` … `proxy.log.2026-10-21_14.gz` cover both windows), but retention is not contractual — measure early or archive the two windows under `/tmp` before they rotate away (the `/tmp/cost/*` outputs cited in the description no longer exist and must be regenerated).
- **Only paid streams carry tokens.** Local and `munitoai-free` streams emit no `tokens=` triple, so "logged tokens" are paid-serving tokens by construction; free-tier share must be read from stream **counts**, never tokens. Any conclusion must state which population it is about.
- **Confounded windows.** The post window contains a proxy restart (2026-10-20 13:10 local) and the context-budget/admission commit series (`c443240c`, `f496626e`, `42f93580`, `ec5514fc`, `242d03f4`, `6999492a`, `a8b56995`) plus `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events) which did not exist pre-change. Single-window before/after cannot separate co-landed changes; use a third reference window and/or per-day series where a cause is ambiguous.
- **Analysis is deterministic only.** Use `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`; do not hand-roll log parsing, and do not edit log data.
- **Investigation scope.** This is an analysis task: fix only a regression that is small and well-understood; larger remediation is filed as a child (AC3).

## Existing state

Measured with the proxy-usage-analysis CLI (log clock = local Europe/Dublin, UTC+1):

| Metric | 2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48 | 2026-10-20 14:44:27 → 2026-10-21 14:44:27 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions / requests | 217 / 12,810 | 228 / 9,137 | −29% requests |
| Logged tokens (input+output) | 421.7 M | 828.5 M | **+96%** |
| Tokens per request | ≈32.9 k | ≈90.7 k | **≈2.8×** |
| Token share by serving entry | `opencode-go-3` 99.98%, `-2` 0.02% | `-3` 99.36%, `-2` 0.20%, `deepseek-flash` 0.44% | — |
| Local streams | 910 | 576 | −37% |
| `munitoai-free` + `munitoai` entry lines | 14,555 | 5,967 | −59% |

Known-relevant capabilities already in the codebase:

- `AnalysisResult.total_tokens()` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` already sums `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` from the `Stream finished ... tokens=prompt/completion/total` lines — the fetch for per-request normalisation exists, but **no report section divides by request count** (checked: no `tokens_per_request` symbol anywhere in the analysis scripts).
- `SessionStats` already records `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `avg_response_size`, `messages` per session, and `CSV_COLUMNS` in `reporting.py` publishes them — so AC1's distribution check needs no new instrumentation.
- `compaction_events` are already collected by the parser (LP-0MTHCTLAF00147IT), so compaction activity can be compared across windows without new parsing.
- Per-dispatch prompt size is already logged: `routing_check ... estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=… cached_ratio=… cache_state=… messages=…` (entry-level, independent of sessions) — e.g. 2,892 `routing_check` lines in the 2026-10-18/19/20 rotated segments sampled vs 7,016 in the 2026-10-20/21 segments. This is the lowest-cost direct test of "prompts got bigger" and needs no new instrumentation.
- Candidate regression surface, from the commit series above: `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (context budget/cached-ratio/prefix bootstrap), `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`, `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`.

## Desired change

1. Regenerate both windows (and at least one additional reference day, e.g. 2026-10-19/20 and 2026-10-22) with the analysis CLI into a stable output dir; archive the CSVs so the numbers are reproducible after rotation.
2. Measure per-dispatch prompt size from `routing_check` lines (`estimated_tokens`, `new_tokens`, `cached_ratio`, `cache_state`, `messages`) for each window — this separates "bigger prompts" from "more dispatches per request" without depending on session boundaries.
3. Compare distributions of `start_context_size`, `avg_context_size`, `max_context_size`, `messages`, `duration_seconds` and per-session token totals across windows; decompose the +407 M delta into (a) more sessions, (b) bigger per-session context, (c) more tokens re-sent per request, (d) **tier mix** — free/local share per request fell from 1.14 to 0.65 `munitoai*` lines per request, so part of the paid-token rise may be traffic re-attributed from the free tier to paid entries rather than a per-request increase — and (e) other/unexplained.
4. Check the accounting hypothesis against `provider_context_exceeded` (2,003 events): confirm each event maps to at most one stream's token triple and that no tokens are counted twice or re-attributed from the free tier.
5. Check the compaction hypothesis: compaction event rate per session across windows, and whether post-compaction prompts grew (i.e. compaction shrinking less or being bypassed).
6. Write the verdict into a comment on LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO with the decomposition table; fix or file the regression (AC3).
7. **Preferred AC4 implementation**: add a tokens-per-request (and total/median per-session token) metric to the analysis report — an `AnalysisResult`/report addition plus a `## Cost / token volume` style section and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — Needs a tokens-per-request aggregate (total input+output ÷ request count) and per-window token trend helper.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — Needs the report section rendering the token-volume / tokens-per-request metric and the CSV columns it depends on.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — Needs CLI wiring only if the metric is exposed as a flag/output.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — Needs unit tests for the new aggregate plus an end-to-end report assertion on fixture logs.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` — Needs the new metric documented.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` / `proxy/config.yaml` — Only if the cause lands in context budget, cached-ratio prefix credit or compaction handling; fix + regression test under `proxy/tests/`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — Only if a routing/budget mechanism is implicated.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVF1FTPQ005ZMYO** — *Verify off-peak low-priority fallback in a live window* (completed): the verification that surfaced the trend; AC5 requires the resolution be recorded there.
- **LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX** — off-peak low-priority fallback epic (the change the verification was testing; not the cause, but the baseline window definition comes from it).
- **LP-0MVF9N3BV00155RI** — *F4: Docs and observability* — introduced the `provider_context_exceeded` observability whose accounting is candidate cause 3.
- **LP-0MVF9N2QL001CDA7** / **LP-0MVF9MY0W002J2N3** — `max_context_tokens` gate implementation and per-entry context-limit tests: the context-budget surface that candidate cause 2 may implicate.
- **LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ** — *Design experiment: validate session compaction gains without quality loss* — relevant to the compaction hypothesis (whether compaction shrinks prompts efficiently).
- **LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B** — *Analyze session context-size distributions from 2026-08-24→26 reports* (completed): direct precedent for AC1 — median/mean/p90/p95/max of session context sizes plus breach counts and trend analysis. Reuse its method rather than inventing one.
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** — *Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File* (completed): relevant to the accounting-artefact hypothesis — a logging gap would distort logged-token volume.
- **Potentially related docs:** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `docs/dev/cached-ratio-prefix-credit.md`, `docs/dev/contention-queue-lease-retention.md`.

Changes that landed inside the post window (verified commit → item mapping):

| Commit | Work item | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `c443240c` | LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ | Prefill-ETA admission guard: stop starting local work that cannot finish in budget |
| `f496626e` | LP-0MVGDUVS6003T2IX | Re-widen local size gates only once cache warmth is proven (capacity-gated) |
| `42f93580` | LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ | Serialise local prefills so one prefill at a time gets the full GPU |
| `ec5514fc` | LP-0MVGGI4Y0003K4AZ | Increase `munitoai-free` `rate_limit_rpm` to 3 (tier-mix candidate) |
| `242d03f4` | LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 | Raise local warm-context routing cap 100K → 120K (and the economic-ceiling ratio) |
| `6999492a` | LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV | Second-turn `cached_ratio` scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn |
| `a8b56995` | LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP | Local dispatch starves returning sessions: contention queue causes local↔remote churn |

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)
- **LP-0MTC87GBV0031F4B** – Analyze session context-size distributions from 2026-08-24→26 reports (completed)
- **LP-0MSNM9BDV007DQXB** – Wire /admin/sessions to index-backed listing (bounded) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+138 more)

> Triage of the automated section: the three work items are legitimate (listed above); the three repository "matches" are false positives — they match boilerplate AC tokens (`ac1`…`ac5`) inside a calibration dataset, not this item's subject. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-LP-0MVIAEARO0001O7R.md`.

## Evidence commands

```bash
# both windows, regenerated and archived (the /tmp/cost/* copies from the discovery pass are gone)
for w in "2026-10-18 14:37:48|2026-10-19 14:37:48|base24" \
         "2026-10-19 14:44:27|2026-10-20 14:44:27|ref24" \
         "2026-10-20 14:44:27|2026-10-21 14:44:27|post24"; do
  IFS='|' read -r s e name <<<"$w"
  python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "$s" --end "$e" --output-dir "$HOME/proxy-usage-reports/cost/$name"
done

# context/message distributions per window
python3 - <<'PY'
import csv, statistics as s
for name in ("base24", "ref24", "post24"):
    p = f"/home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/cost/{name}/standard_sessions.csv"
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(p)))
    for col in ("start_context_size", "max_context_size", "messages", "duration_seconds"):
        vals = [int(float(r[col])) for r in rows if r.get(col)]
        print(name, col, len(vals), round(s.median(vals)), round(s.mean(vals)))
PY

# accounting check: per-entry token triples and provider_context_exceeded events
zcat /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_15.gz /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-20_21.gz \
    /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log-2026-10-21_00.gz /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-21_07.gz \
  | grep "^.*entry=opencode-go" | grep -o "tokens=[0-9]*/[0-9]*/[0-9]*" | head

grep -ch "provider_context_exceeded" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | paste -sd+ | bc

# per-dispatch prompt size (independent of session boundaries)
zcat /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-2[01]_*.gz | grep -o "routing_check .*estimated_tokens=[0-9]*" \
  | grep -o "estimated_tokens=[0-9]*" | cut -d= -f2 | sort -n \
  | awk '{s+=$1; a[NR]=$1} END{print "n="NR, "median="a[int(NR/2)], "mean="int(s/NR)}'
```

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — co-landed changes.** Seven commits plus a proxy restart sit inside the post window; a single before/after pair cannot attribute cleanly. Mitigation: add reference windows and a per-day trend; if attribution stays ambiguous, AC2's "unexplained with residual" branch is the honest outcome.
- **Risk — log loss.** Rotated logs are not guaranteed; measurements must be archived. Mitigation: run the CLI early and copy CSVs into the work-item comment/summary.
- **Risk — scope creep into proxy tuning.** Fixing every mechanism noticed would balloon the item. Mitigation: fix only small, well-understood regressions; file the rest as children (AC3).
- **Risk — tier-mix confounding.** The free-tier line share fell faster than requests (`munitoai*` lines per request 1.14 → 0.65), so part of the paid-token rise may be re-attribution rather than growth. Mitigation: decompose by tier before concluding (Desired change step 2d).
- **Risk — metric theatre.** A tokens-per-request number without a baseline/target will not catch drift. Mitigation: publish a per-day series (AC4) rather than a single scalar.
- **Assumption — "logged tokens" means paid-serving tokens.** Only opencode/deepseek streams emit `tokens=` triples; conclusions are scoped accordingly and free-tier share is reported from counts.
- **Assumption — both windows are still re-measurable** from `/var/log/llama-proxy` (verified 2026-10-22); if a window has rotated away, the recorded figures from the description are the fallback baseline and that limitation is stated.
- **Assumption — no operator-requested scope beyond the named candidates** was given; four-window/tier-mix comparison and the AC4 metric are the assumed floor. The serving-tier-mix candidate was added by the agent because the free-tier line count fell 59% against a 29% request drop; it is not a new requirement, only a fourth hypothesis for the same question.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (goal, two measured windows, named candidate causes, ACs, evidence commands) was sufficient to draft the brief.
- Assumption recorded (agent, not operator): AC4 is implemented in this item rather than merely proposed — the metric is small, lives in the existing analysis package, and is the only durable defence against a repeat. Source: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` already computes token totals, so the addition is a report/aggregate change.

- Assumption recorded (agent): issue type stays `task` (investigation) at priority `medium`; reassign upward if a regression is confirmed.

data.description:
# Prefill-ETA admission guard ignores occupancy: admits queue waits that are guaranteed to time out

## Problem statement

The prefill-ETA admission guard (`proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) was added to stop exactly the failure mode observed today: a request parks in the contention queue for up to `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (120 s), produces nothing, and then falls back to a remote provider anyway. It compares the caller's **own** projected prefill (`eta_prefill_seconds`) against the wait budget — but not the time until a slot actually becomes available. With prefills serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), another prefill is already in flight, so the true newcomer wait is its own prefill **plus** the in-flight prefill.

The proxy already computes that larger quantity and publishes it: `/llama/local/status` serves `queue_eta_seconds = prefill_eta_seconds x (busy_slots + 1)`. The guard simply does not use it. Result: the guard's own published estimate can exceed the budget while the guard still admits.

## Measured evidence (2026-10-21, window 14:56–16:49, post-restart)

Source: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`.

- 302 `contention_queue_wait` events → 40 `contention_queue_dispatch` (13 %) vs **261 `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` (86 %)**.
- **215 of the 261 (82 %) burned the full 120 s budget** before falling back remote; aggregate wasted wait **25,804 s (7.2 h)** inside a 1.9 h wall-clock window.
- **247 of 325 full-budget losses entered the queue with `saturation=prefill`** (only 35 with `saturation=generating`) — the prefill gate, not the decode pool, is the dominant blocker.
- Admitting guard ETA distribution (n=307): median **49 s**, p75 58 s, max 100 s — i.e. consistently "within budget" against 120 s, while the real wait includes the in-flight prefill ahead of it.
- Smoking gun (15:10:45 → 15:10:57): `/llama/local/status` published `prefill_eta_seconds=43.0 queue_eta_seconds=129.0` (129 s > 120 s budget); 12 s later the guard logged `local_admission_guard decision=admit reason=within_budget eta_prefill_s=32.2 budget_s=120.0` and queued the request, which then waited the full budget and fell back remote.
- Compounding blindness: **188** `prefill_progress_unobservable` / `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold` warnings in the same window — `lease_extended_during_prefill ... progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` repeatedly extends a lease with no visibility of prefill progress or liveness.

## Users

- As an operator, I want a request that cannot be served locally within the queue budget to fall back **immediately**, so the caller is not stalled 120 s for a guaranteed-loss wait and remote latency is paid late instead of on time.
- As a client dispatcher (herdr downtime worker, `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`), I want the proxy's admission decision to be consistent with the ETA fields it publishes, so client-side pacing is a defence in depth rather than the only defence.

## Desired change

1. **Use the occupancy-aware estimate at admission.** The guard decision must compare the *projected wait* (`queue_eta`-style: own prefill plus the remaining service of the occupied/capped prefill gate) against `wait_budget_seconds`, not the own-prefill term alone. Reuse the single shared estimator in `prefill_eta.py`; do not add a second ETA implementation.
2. **Prefer measured remaining service time where available.** The occupancy term should use the observed in-flight prefill's elapsed time and calibrated per-token prefill cost (falling back to `eta x (busy + 1)` when progress is unobservable).
3. **Fix the unobservable-progress path.** `prefill_progress_unobservable` (188 in-window) must not leave the lease extended blindly: when neither per-slot progress nor the `is_processing` liveness signal is available, the guard must treat the in-flight prefill as occupying the gate for at least the calibrated estimate, so waiters are not admitted against a phantom "free soon".
4. **Keep the fail-open contract.** Uncalibrated bucket, missing budget, or `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off` must behave exactly as today (admit; never reject on a guess).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — occupancy-aware refusal:** when the projected wait (`queue_eta_seconds`-equivalent, including in-flight prefill) exceeds `wait_budget_seconds` while the own-prefill ETA is within budget, the guard returns `admit=False` with `reason=eta_exceeds_budget` (or a new explicit reason) and the request falls through to the next provider without queueing. Covered by a unit test using a calibrated fixture where own ETA < budget < projected wait.
2. **AC2 — self-consistency:** a test asserts the guard's projected wait agrees with the value published as `queue_eta_seconds` by `status_estimate` for the same `(model, tokens, busy_slots)` inputs, so the two can never drift apart again.
3. **AC3 — fail-open preserved:** uncalibrated bucket, absent budget, `high` priority, and `policy=observe` all still admit (regression tests); `policy=off` does not evaluate the guard.
4. **AC4 — lease/progress:** a calibrated scenario with `prefill_progress_unobservable` (no per-slot progress, `alive=False`, `in_flight=True`) treats the in-flight prefill as occupying the gate for at least the calibrated estimate, and the decision is logged with the occupancy evidence (tests).
5. **AC5 — measured effect:** replay against the 2026-10-21 14:56–16:49 window (261 queued fallbacks, 215 at full budget, 247 prefill-saturated) reports in the work item how many of the 261 would now be refused immediately (saving their queue wait) and how many would still be admitted and dispatched, with the aggregate saved wait in seconds. The replay must show zero **lost** dispatches (i.e. no request that would have succeeded after queueing is refused) or justify each exception.
6. **AC6 — logging/observability:** the admission log line carries own ETA, occupancy term, projected wait, budget, in-flight prefill count and the resulting decision, so the failure mode is diagnosable from the log alone.
7. **AC7 — docs:** `proxy/docs/routing.md` (or the admission-guard section it references) and the `proxy/config.yaml` comment block for `local_admission_guard_policy` describe the occupancy-aware model and the `queue_eta` self-consistency requirement.
8. **AC8 — suite:** full project test suite passes via the test skill.

## Constraints

- Fail-open only: the change may refuse *additional* doomed admissions, never admit more than today.
- One estimator: no duplicate ETA maths; `prefill_eta.py` remains the single source of truth.
- No new configuration knob unless strictly required; if one is needed, name it, clamp it, and document it.
- Behaviour must remain correct for `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 0` (gate disabled → occupancy term collapses to the slot pool).
- Out of scope: reducing `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, and the ctx-size/slot trade-off (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM AC6).

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `evaluate_admission`, `estimate_prefill_seconds`, `status_estimate`, `per_slot_prefill_eta_seconds`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, `_prefill_admission_guard` call site, `_local_slot_saturation`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_get_prefill_lease_config`, lease extension on prefill progress.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `get_llama_local_status` (`queue_eta_seconds`, `prefill_budget_seconds`).
- `proxy/tests/` — admission-guard and contention-queue tests.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX** (ContextHub) — herdr downtime dispatcher paces to `local_prefills_in_flight` / `prefill_gate_waiters` and defers when `queue_eta_seconds > prefill_budget_seconds`. This item is the *server-side* counterpart; the two are complementary, not alternatives (84 % of the 2026-10-21 queued-fallback events came from non-downtime agent/LAN traffic that no client-side pacing covers).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (this item corrects its model).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`); publishes the gate fields.
- LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI — truthful capacity payload (`prefill_eta_seconds`, `queue_eta_seconds`, `prefill_budget_seconds`).
- LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI — contention-queue wake predicate must account for prefill in flight.
- LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D — bounded cross-session contention queue.
- LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP — lease-owner retention priority.
- LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (AC6) — local ctx-size / slot-count evaluation (1 slot x 262144 co-change).

## Risks

- **Over-refusal:** a pessimistic occupancy term could refuse waits that would have won. Mitigation: AC5 replay must show zero lost dispatches (or justify exceptions), and the change is fail-open by construction.
- **Stale in-flight estimate:** the calibrated per-token prefill cost varies with cache state; the occupancy term must use observed elapsed time for the in-flight prefill where possible.
- **Duplicate-logic drift:** mitigated by AC2's single-estimator consistency test.

## Assumptions

- `queue_eta_seconds = eta x (busy + 1)` is an acceptable upper-bound proxy for the remaining-gate-wait term when per-slot progress is unobservable (as measured, it already flagged the 129 s > 120 s case correctly).
- `saturation=prefill` in the queue-wait log line identifies gate waits reliably enough to segment the replay (247/325 of the losses).

## Evidence appendix

Reproduce the window with:

```
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
    --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --start "2026-10-21 14:56:00"
```

then `grep -E 'contention_queue_(wait|dispatch|fallback_after_queue)|local_admission_guard'` on the same window.

# Proxy: atomic local-admission reservations + explicit fallback intent (X-Local-Preference / X-Local-Route)

## Problem statement

Today a client that wants to keep its work local has no way to *claim* local capacity before sending: it can poll `/llama/local/status` (racy — two clients can both see the same idle window; observed queue depth reached 7 while `available_slots` still reported 2 with the prefill gate saturated) and it can only learn it lost **after** the proxy has silently fallen back to a remote provider (`X-Provider: opencode` is set only post-hoc). The measured consequence (2026-10-21 14:56→17:00, 372 queue events): 261 requests queued and then went remote anyway, 215 of them after the full 120 s budget (25,804 s aggregate wasted wait).

The correct behaviour, per operator direction: **the client must not send work it cannot start.** That decision has to be made atomically — a serialised prefill gate is a single ticket that poll-and-send cannot allocate among N clients — and it has to be made *before* the work is sent. This item adds the server-side handshake; the client side is herdr `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (ContextHub) plus its reservation follow-up.

Prerequisite: `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware admission guard) — the reservation must share the guard's model or it inherits the same blind spot.

## Goal / users

- As a client dispatcher (herdr downtime worker, other agents, LAN clients), I want to reserve local capacity for a specific request before sending it, so I never queue behind a doomed wait and never silently go remote.
- As an operator, I want the proxy to answer "is my work going to run local, and if not why not" **before** the request runs, and to let me express per-request intent (`local-only` / `prefer-local` / `remote-ok`) instead of guessing.

## Desired change

1. **`POST /llama/local/reserve`** — atomic admission reservation (a gate ticket), sharing the single estimator/occupancy model from `prefill_eta.py`:
   - Request: `{estimated_tokens, session_id?, priority?, cache_state?, ttl_seconds?}`.
   - `200 {"admit": true, "reservation_id", "projected_wait_s", "ttl_s"}` — the ticket is claimed: a follow-up request carrying `X-Local-Reservation: <id>` dispatches without re-checking or queueing, subject to TTL.
   - `429 {"admit": false, "reason", "queue_eta_s", "budget_s", "retry_after_s", "X-Local-Admission*"}` — refused immediately with the reason and a retry hint; the client defers.
   - Tickets are TTL-bound (default ~5–10 s), single-use, cancellable via `DELETE /llama/local/reserve/<id>`; unclaimed tickets expire and the gate is released. A stale/missing reservation on the follow-up request falls back to today's ordinary path (never a hard failure).
   - `local-only` semantics (see 2) also available as `dry_run=true` — verdict without claiming the ticket.
2. **`X-Local-Preference: local-only | prefer-local | remote-ok`** request header, documented and additive:
   - `local-only` — never fall back remote; if the request cannot be admitted within the wait budget the proxy returns the 429 admission response **even when remote providers exist** (today it only emits that 429 when the whole chain is exhausted).
   - `prefer-local` — default, today's behaviour (queue briefly, else remote).
   - `remote-ok` — skip the local route entirely (for background/low-priority work).
3. **Response transparency headers on every response:** `X-Local-Route: local|remote|refused` and, on remote or refused, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: <reason>` so a client can observe its loss at the moment it happens, not after.
4. **Admission guard call-site integration:** `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` and the lease-owner retention path use the same verdict as `/reserve` (single source of truth).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — reserve end-to-end:** a calibrated-fixture test asserts reserve returns a ticket when the occupancy-aware projected wait fits the budget, and that a follow-up request with the ticket dispatches local without queueing (assert no `contention_queue_wait` log for that request).
2. **AC2 — reserve refusal:** a calibrated-fixture test asserts reserve returns 429 with `reason`, `queue_eta_s`, `budget_s`, `retry_after_s` when the projected wait exceeds the budget, and that the refused request never enters the contention queue.
3. **AC3 — TTL and cancellation:** an expired or cancelled ticket is not honoured (falls back to ordinary path); a cancelled reservation releases the gate for the next ticket (tests).
4. **AC4 — local-only:** with `X-Local-Preference: local-only`, a request that would fall back remote instead receives the 429 admission response (with retry-after), and this behaviour is exercised when remote providers ARE available (tests).
5. **AC5 — remote-ok:** `remote-ok` never attempts the local route (assert no local attempt in the providers chain) — regression test.
6. **AC6 — route headers:** successful local responses carry `X-Local-Route: local`; remote-served responses carry `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` matching the recorded fallback reason; refused requests carry `X-Local-Route: refused` (tests).
7. **AC7 — single estimator:** the reserve verdict and the admission-guard verdict are computed by the same function; a test asserts identical outcomes for identical inputs (mirrors `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` AC2).
8. **AC8 — fail-open/backcompat:** unknown `X-Local-Preference` values, missing fields, and proxies/clients without the endpoint behave exactly as today; the endpoint and headers are additive. Uncalibrated estimator → reserve admits (never rejects on a guess).
9. **AC9 — measured effect:** replay against the 2026-10-21 14:56–16:49 window reports how many of the 261 queued fallbacks would now be refused at reserve (saving their queue wait), how many follow-up dispatches would still succeed, and the aggregate wait saved; zero lost dispatches (or each exception justified).
10. **AC10 — docs & suite:** `proxy/docs/routing.md` and the `proxy/config.yaml` comment block document the handshake, the header contract, and the interaction with `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`/`_max_depth`; full project suite passes via the test skill.

## Constraints

- The reservation shares the occupancy-aware guard; it must not duplicate ETA maths (`prefill_eta.py` is the single source of truth).
- Fail-open: any uncertainty (uncalibrated, missing budget, `policy=observe|off`) admits like today; refusal requires a calibrated verdict AND explicit caller intent (`local-only`) or a genuinely exceeded budget.
- No new polling loops; no changes to `session_slot_pool_size` or ctx-size (that is `LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM` AC6).
- Security/concurrency: ticket IDs are unpredictable; reservations are per-gate (the prefill gate), scoped per provider endpoint; a ticket may not bypass the context clamp or context-bypass rules.
- Out of scope: client-side adoption (herdr `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` + ContextHub reservation follow-up), and the contention-queue sweep (`LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R`).

## Key files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — new `/llama/local/reserve` route(s), `X-Local-Preference` parsing, route headers.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — shared occupancy verdict (with `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV`).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — guard call site, `local-only` skip-remote path, response headers.
- `proxy/proxy/priority.py` — preference/priority interaction (`local-only` vs `high` never-queues).
- `proxy/tests/` — reserve, headers, fail-open tests.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` — **blocks this item**: occupancy-aware admission guard (prerequisite; share its verdict).
- `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` — blocked-by this item: contention-queue sweep once reservations land.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (ContextHub) — client-side pacing counterpart; comment LP-C0MV… (on that item) asserts the one-item-per-idle-window requirement.
- `LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ`, `LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ`, `LP-0MVGDUVGE0024YAI` — prefill ETA guard, serialisation gate fields, truthful capacity payload.
- `LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D`, `LP-0MVI2VRT2000V1AP`, `LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI` — contention queue, lease retention, prefill-aware wake.

## Risks

- **Ticket misuse / hoarding:** a client reserving and not sending would starve others. Mitigation: short TTL, single-use, cancellation endpoint, monitoring of `reserved-but-unused` (additive status field).
- **Over-refusal on `local-only`:** a wrong verdict means remote latency, not a failure — and fail-open design means refusal needs calibration.
- **Drift between `status`, guard, and reserve:** mitigated by the single-estimator AC7.

# Contention-queue sweep: collapse depth/wait once reservations land

## Problem statement

The contention queue converts wait time into a chance of staying local. On the
current 60 s budget the conversion has already failed: in the 3.3 h after the
120 s → 60 s change went live, 180 local queue events produced **38 wins and
142 losses, every loss at the full 60 s** — 8 705 s (≈2.4 h) of dead wait that
ended on a remote provider anyway. The two remaining knobs
(`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `contention_queue_max_depth: 8`) are
load-shedding knobs, and neither separates a slow-but-winnable wait from a
hopeless one.

Once cooperating clients reserve capacity (`POST /llama/local/reserve`,
`LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`, live since 2026-10-21), the queue no longer needs to be
the primary waiting mechanism: it only has to be a small safety net for
stragglers and non-cooperating clients.

## Users

- As an **operator**, I want the fallback queue to be a bounded straggler net,
  not a 60 s parking lot, so dead local wait stops competing with real local
  work.
- As a **cooperating client** (herdr dispatcher), I want my only waits to be
  ticket-backed reserved waits, so I can plan around a wait I hold rather than
  an invisible proxy-side park.
- As a **non-cooperating client**, I still want a short grace window before the
  proxy detours to a remote provider, so a slot that frees within seconds is
  still usable.

## Evidence appendix (measurements)

**Current 60 s era** — `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`, 2026-10-22 19:00 →
22:18 (3.3 h, the window since the proxy restarted on the 60 s config):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| queue events (`contention_queue_dispatch` + `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`) | 180 |
| wins | 38 (21 %) |
| losses | 142 (79 %) — **all** at full budget (`queued_duration≈60.0s`) |
| aggregate dead wait | 8 705 s (≈2.4 h) |
| win wait p50 / p75 / p90 / max | 39.5 s / 48.1 s / 59.8 s / 112.9 s |
| loss reason split | 95 `local_lease_active`, 47 none |

Retained wins by candidate budget (same window): 10 s → 6/38 (16 %),
15 s → 6/38 (16 %), **20 s → 9/38 (24 %)**, **30 s → 13/38 (34 %)**,
45 s → 23/38 (60 %), 60 s → 35/38 (92 %).

**Prior 120 s era** (for continuity, from the creating comment): 2026-10-21
14:56 → 17:00, 372 queue events — 43 wins (median wait 65 s) versus 329 losses,
283 (86 %) of which would have needed ≥120 s under any cap; 261 requests
queued and then went remote, 215 after the full budget (25 804 s aggregate
wait); queue depth reached 7 in-window.

**Reservation adoption** — server endpoint shipped (`LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`,
`completed`), status payload exposes `reserved_issued/used/cancelled/expired`,
and the dispatch path logs `local_admission_reserve_claimed`. Observed usage in
the last 24 h of `proxy.log*`: **0** claimed tickets, `reserved_issued: 0`. The
client-side item `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` is still `open`/`idea`, so no client
sends `X-Local-Reservation` / `X-Local-Preference` yet.

**Guard activity in the same 3.3 h window**: 870 refusals — 376 on the queue
path (`reason=eta_exceeds_budget`) and 494 on the direct free-slot path
(`reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`). The ETA guard is already doing the bulk
of the shedding; the *residual* losses that still park for the full budget sit
mostly on the lease-retention branch (`reason=local_lease_active`, 95 of 142).

## Desired change (the sweep)

1. **Target values** — `proxy/config.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30   # was 60 (was 120 in LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO)
   contention_queue_max_depth: 2           # was 8
   ```

   30 s retains a third of current wins while capping dead wait at 30 s; depth
   2 keeps a straggler net without the observed 7-deep parking lot. Both values
   stay inside the existing clamps (`wait` ∈ [1, guardrail], `depth` ∈ [1, 16]).

2. **Trigger (decoupled from client adoption — operator decision 2026-10-22)**
   — the sweep is *not* gated on `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`. Preconditions: the
   reservation endpoint is live (met 2026-10-21) **and** a ≥24 h pre-flip
   baseline exists at 60 s/depth 8 (≈55 queue events/h → ~1 300 events/day;
   the 3.3 h intake window is the seed, extend before flipping).
   Post-flip observation: 7 days / ≥1 000 queue events.

3. **Flip criteria** (measured over the observation window against the 24 h
   pre-flip baseline) — keep the sweep if **all** hold:
   - aggregate dead wait per hour falls by ≥50 %;
   - residual queue wins stay ≥20 % of queue events (i.e. the net still
     converts something);
   - remote dispatch volume rises by <20 % relative (no flood of paid
     fallbacks).

4. **Rollback** — revert the two values to 60 / 8, restart the proxy (config
   change requires a restart), and record the observed metrics in this item.
   `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` and
   `contention_queue_policy: queue` are unchanged; the lease grace stays above
   the new budget so a returning session still re-queues as retained.

5. **Residual-queue telemetry (reporting, not a gate)** — a windowed report
   counting (a) ticket-backed dispatches (`local_admission_reserve_claimed`),
   (b) residual queue wins at or below the sweep budget
   (`contention_queue_dispatch … queued_duration=`), (c) residual queue losses
   and their aggregate wait (`contention_queue_fallback_after_queue …
   queued_duration=`), split by `reason` so lease-active losses are visible
   separately (95/142 today). Source: the log lines, **not** new status
   counters — cumulative counters were deliberately removed in
   `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` and log parsing is the established consumer pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger (endpoint live + ≥24 h 60 s baseline, decoupled from client
   adoption per operator decision 2026-10-22), the 7-day observation window,
   the flip criteria above, and the two-line rollback with proxy restart;
   each value justified by the win/loss distributions in the evidence
   appendix.
2. **AC2 — single-source budget.** The shortened budget reaches the admission
   guard's `wait_budget_seconds` and `POST /llama/local/reserve`'s budget
   through the **same** resolver (`prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds`) — no
   second constant, no per-call default — with tests asserting that
   `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 30` is what both the guard and the
   reservation endpoint compare against, and that `depth: 2` is accepted and
   clamped only outside [1, 16].
3. **AC3 — residual-queue telemetry.** A windowed report (script + test) emits
   (a) ticket-backed dispatch count, (b) residual queue wins at or below the
   sweep budget, (c) residual queue losses with aggregate wait and a `reason`
   split (lease-active vs other) for a stated window; the report is run and its
   numbers recorded on this item when the sweep is evaluated. Ticket counts are
   reported, not used as a flip gate. Data comes from the existing log events
   (reusing `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a library
   where practical); **no new status counters** — `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` removed
   the cumulative ones on purpose.
4. **AC4 — tests / validation.** Unit tests cover the swept values end to end:
   config validation accepts 30/2, the queue resolver returns 30 s, a waiter
   beyond depth 2 falls back immediately instead of enqueueing, and a waiter
   that exceeds 30 s falls back at 30 s; fixtures/tests that assume the
   60 s / 8 defaults are updated rather than left stale.
5. **AC5 — docs.** `proxy/config.yaml` comments and `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   describe the queue as a straggler safety net for non-cooperating clients,
   with reservations as the primary cooperative path, and record the
   60 → 30 s / 8 → 2 change with its measurement dates, flip criteria and
   rollback.
6. **AC6 — documentation & suite.** All related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki
   or docs site entries; full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Constraints

- Fail-open semantics of the admission guard are unchanged (uncalibrated →
  admit).
- One budget, one resolver: no new knob, no per-reason budget (operator
  decision 2026-10-22); the lease-active split is a *reporting* dimension
  only.
- Out of scope: queue removal (a zero-wait proxy has no local concurrency
  tolerance at all), slot count, ctx-size, the ETA guard's model, and client
  reservation adoption (`WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`).
- Changing either value requires a proxy restart; the sweep must be applied in
  a quiet window and announced in the item comment trail.

## Existing state

- `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `contention_queue_max_depth: 8`,
  `contention_queue_policy: queue`, `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300`
  (`proxy/config.yaml` ~1651–1683).
- `_get_contention_queue_config()` clamps wait to
  [1, `session_guardrail_max_runtime_seconds`] and depth to [1, 16], logging
  and coercing invalid values.
- `prefill_eta.wait_budget_seconds(config, priority)` is the single resolver
  used by the guard, `/reserve` and `provider.py`.
- Queue telemetry exists as log events only (`contention_queue_dispatch`,
  `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`); reservation counters exist as
  process-lifetime counters in `/llama/local/status`, so a *windowed* report
  must come from the logs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — sweep the two values, rewrite the surrounding comment
  block (line ~1651) with the new evidence and the rollback note.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `wait_budget_seconds()`; assert the single
  resolver path (no change expected beyond a comment).
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `_get_contention_queue_config()` clamps; confirm
  30/2 pass through unchanged.
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — budget sourced from the resolver
  (comment / assertion only if it hard-codes anything).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — `wait_for_local_slot()` depth-cap
  behaviour (immediate fallback beyond depth).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — status payload (`contention_queue_depth`, live
  depth and reservation counters); no new cumulative counters are added here
  (see `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP`).
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_llama_local_status.py` — updates for the swept defaults.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — queue/reservation description and the recorded
  change (lines ~674, 731, 897–899).
- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (new) — windowed residual-queue
  report for AC3; parses `proxy.log*` and may import
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` as a library (read-only
  use; that skill's files are not edited here). Modelled on
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`. Extending the daily proxy usage report with the
  same breakdown is a possible follow-up, not part of this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lost local wins become remote spend.** 30 s converts ~29 of the current 38
  wins per 3.3 h into remote dispatches; the flip criteria cap that at +20 %
  remote volume and the rollback is two lines. *Assumption (operator,
  2026-10-22):* the dead-wait saving is worth the trade even before clients
  reserve.
- **Reservations unused today.** No client sends `X-Local-Reservation` yet, so
  the "queue is only for stragglers" premise is aspirational until
  `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` lands; the sweep is justified on queue economics
  instead, and AC3 keeps ticket counts visible so the premise can be re-checked
  when adoption arrives.
- **Lease-active losses dominate the residual (95/142).** A 30 s budget shortens
  the wait for returning lease owners too. Reported separately (AC3); a
  per-reason budget is explicitly out of scope (would be a second mechanism
  needing its own evidence).
- **Guard interaction.** The ETA guard fires before queueing; a shorter budget
  makes it stricter (fewer queued waits, more direct fallbacks), so the
  observed win rate may fall below the 34 % projection. Tracked by the flip
  criteria, which require ≥20 %.
- **Observation-window bias.** The 3.3 h intake window was dominated by
  audit/batch sessions (`session=audit-…`), which are long and prefill-heavy;
  the 34 % retained-win projection is therefore a lower bound for interactive
  work and an upper bound for audit bursts. Hence the requirement for a ≥24 h
  pre-flip baseline before applying the change.
- **Restart cost.** Applying the change restarts the proxy and drops in-flight
  local state; schedule in a quiet window.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Extra opportunities found (e.g. lease-active budget,
  windowed metrics in `/llama/local/status`) are recorded as linked work items,
  not absorbed here.

## Related work

- Depends on: `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (reservation endpoint — `completed`).
- Related: `LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO` (120 s → 60 s, the current baseline),
  `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware guard; holds the win/loss
  distributions), `LP-0MVIQ0F8T002FS42` (guard on the direct path),
  `LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D` (queue origin), `LP-0MTF6EVLW007PEHN` (the opposite
  move: raise caps), `LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP` (cumulative queue counters removed —
  logs are the telemetry contract), `LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD` (epic: local tail
  latency), `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` (client reservation adoption — related, not
  blocking).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MTF6EVLW007PEHN** – Raise cheap-mode contention queue caps (wait 60->120s, depth 4->8) (completed)
- **LP-0MU4NACW9001WKBP** – Remove useless contention queue cumulative counters (completed)
- **LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20** – Reserve free-tier request budget for in-progress sessions, cap the wait at 15s (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0msorqvk50012q4d, 0mvicd2yw004djpv, 0mvikpcsg002b0nl, ac1, ac2 (+158 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac9 (+148 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac9 (+148 more)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (trigger).** Reservations shipped 2026-10-21 but no client sends them
  (0 `local_admission_reserve_claimed` in 24 h; `reserved_issued: 0`;
  `WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8` still `idea`). Wait for client adoption, decouple, or
  split? — **Answer (operator, 2026-10-22): B — decouple.** Sweep on queue
  economics alone; ticket counts become reporting (AC3), not a gate.
  Evidence: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` 24 h scan; `/llama/local/status`
  reservation counters; `wl show WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8`. Agent recommendation was

  every loss already burning the full budget.
- **Q3 (lease-active waiters).** 95 of 142 full-budget losses are
  `reason=local_lease_active`: one global value, or a longer budget for that

data.description:
# Epic: minimise local LLM tail latency (prefill-bound first-byte tails)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator/agent driving the proxy, I want a local Qwen3 request to either
answer inside a bounded budget or be routed remote quickly, so that the
multi-minute stalls that dominate the local tail disappear and the worst-case
latency across the whole provider set is bounded by tens of seconds rather than
minutes.

## Measured baseline (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

All figures from `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` and `llama-server.log`.

| Signal | Baseline |
|---|---|
| Local dispatch → first byte (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`, n=606) | p50 **8.9 s**, p90 **96.5 s**, p99 **443 s**, max **592 s** |
| Local dispatches with first byte > 60 s / > 120 s | **91** / **48** of 606 |
| Same, `cache_state=warm` subset (n=419) | p90 **88.7 s**, max 592 s |
| llama-server prompt-eval duration | p50 16 s, p90 **189 s**, max **591 s** |
| Prompt-eval throughput | p10 **77 t/s**, p50 211 t/s (20 k+ batches), p90 302 t/s |
| `local_admission_guard` | 1 965 admit (`within_budget`) / **415 reject** (`eta_exceeds_budget`) |
| `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` | **1 481** (`reason=local_lease_active`) + 252 unlabelled, all after the full 120 s wait |
| `orphan_cleanup` vs `lease_verified_active` | **298** vs **6** |
| Local streams > 60 s that were orphan-cleaned mid-span yet finished later | **81** of 118 |
| `contention_queue_wait ... saturation=` samples | **1 827** prefill vs 468 generating |
| `prefill_progress_unobservable` | 1 242 |

Interpretation: `dispatch_to_first_byte` ≈ total local response time, so the tail
is **prefill**, not decode. A 40–80 k-token prefill costs 130–500 s at the
measured throughput, `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` makes one such prefill
block everything behind it, and the lease bookkeeping frees slots that are still
working (298 cleanups vs 6 verified alive).

## Scope

**In scope** — five children:

1. `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` 120 → 60.
2. Prefill-ETA guard on the **direct (free-slot) dispatch** path.
3. Orphan-cleanup / `/slots` liveness fix (fail-closed, cancel upstream).
4. llama-server `ubatch-size` 1024 → 2048 (benchmark-gated).
5. ETA-aware admission ordering + prefill heartbeat + prefill deadline.

**Explicitly out of scope** (do not fold into a child):

- **Warm-cache threshold is unchanged** — `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`
  stays 120000 and `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` stays 0.4578.
- **No TTS isolation** — TTS stays on the shared GPU; child 4 is the ubatch
  change only.
- No prompt-compaction change (`compaction_trigger_ratio` stays 0) and no
  slot-pool change (`session_slot_pool_size` stays 2).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` over a ≥24 h deployed window: p90 ≤ 45 s
   (baseline 96.5 s), p99 ≤ 120 s (baseline 443 s), max ≤ 180 s (baseline 592 s).
2. Zero local dispatches whose first byte exceeds the configured local wait
   budget (baseline 48 > 120 s): every over-budget projection is refused
   up-front and routed remote.
3. Orphan churn collapses: `orphan_cleanup` ≤ 5 % of local dispatches (baseline
   298 cleanups ≈ 49 % of 606) and **zero** streams that are orphan-cleaned and
   then go on to finish (baseline 81).
4. No regression: remote provider p50/p90 unchanged, local decode throughput and
   aggregate prefill tokens/s not reduced, full test suite green.
5. Each child lands with its own tests, config/docs updates, and a measured
   before/after recorded on the item (reuse the LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD measurement
   approach).
6. `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` and
   `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` are unchanged at completion.

## Risks / notes

- **Measurement contamination:** child 4 needs a llama-server restart, which
  empties the prompt cache and biases first-byte stats cold. Sequence child 4's
  measurement window so it is not mixed with the others, and record the
  restart in the child's comment.
- **Single budget source:** children 1, 2 and 5 all reason about the same wait
  budget (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`). Do not introduce a second,
  competing budget; the ETA estimator and the guard must stay one implementation.
- **Load shifting:** refusing more local work pushes traffic onto rate-limited
  remote tiers (munitoai-free 3 rpm, opencode). Watch 429s and fallback counts in
  the same window; a latency win that produces remote 429 storms is not a win.
- **Budget values:** 60 s for the contention queue was chosen from a separate
  investigation (see child 1); 30 s was the fallback if the evidence disagreed.
  This analysis found no evidence contradicting 60 s.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (queue-entry only today).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`).
- LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — `/slots` unobservable during long prefills.
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 — progress unobservable under load.
- LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8 — watchdog released the lease but never cancelled upstream.
- LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2 — active-stream verification in orphan cleanup.
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement of local admission impact (reuse its
  methodology for the before/after on each child).
- LP-0MV9UNGEB009XUZ5 — slot pool fixed at 2.

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a request that cannot get a local slot to spend at most
**60 s** in the contention queue before it falls through to a remote provider,
so the dead waiting time on the local path halves without losing the
lease-owner retention benefit.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` fired **1 481** times with
  `reason=local_lease_active` (plus 252 with no reason), every one after
  `queued_duration=120.00s` — i.e. the full budget was spent and the request
  went remote anyway.
- The config comment for `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` already records
  the same pattern from the 2026-10-19→20 measurement: 4 947 of 5 805 queued
  waits (85 %) were abandoned, and the prefill-ETA guard exists precisely
  because "the wait is a guaranteed loss".
- Local first byte is p50 8.9 s but p90 96.5 s / p99 443 s (n=606), i.e. the
  queue is not absorbing the tail, it is relocating it.

## Proposed change

Single knob:

```yaml
server:
  contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60   # was 120
```

- Keep `contention_queue_max_depth: 8` and
  `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` unchanged.
- Keep `contention_queue_policy: queue` unchanged.
- No new knobs; no code change expected beyond config/docs if the value is read
  per request (confirm on implementation; document if a proxy restart is
  required).

**Why 60 and not 30:** a separate investigation concluded 60 s is the optimum
for this queue. This analysis has no evidence that contradicts it — the queued
population is dominated by retained sessions whose prompt cache is warm (the
case the retention rule exists to protect), where a 60 s wait can still succeed
— so 60 is adopted. 30 s is the documented fallback if the measurement after
this change shows the queue is still pure loss (i.e. the abandoned share does
not fall).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `server.contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` is 60 in `proxy/config.yaml`, with
   the comment updated to record the baseline (1 481 full-120 s fallbacks) and
   the reason for the value.
2. A queued local request never waits longer than 60 s before falling back
   (test covering the timeout path).
3. Lease-owner retention behaviour is unchanged: the existing retention tests
   (`contention_queue_retention` / `lease_grace`) pass unmodified.
4. Docs updated (`proxy/docs/routing.md` or wherever the contention queue is
   described) and the restart/reload requirement documented.
5. A ≥24 h deployed measurement shows `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`
   `queued_duration` bounded by 60 s and no increase in fallbacks *per request*;
   record numbers on this item.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- Shortening the wait moves some retained sessions to remote earlier; if the
  remote tier is rate-limited (munitoai-free 3 rpm) this can produce 429s.
  Watch 429s and `Fallback triggered ... rate_limited` in the same window.
- If the ETA guard (LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) rejects prefill projections above the
  budget, a shorter queue only changes how long the request takes to discover
  it cannot be served — that is the intended behaviour.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (budget consumer).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (why slots are busy for minutes).
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want **any** local dispatch whose projected prefill cannot
finish inside the local wait budget to be refused up-front — even when a slot is
free — so we never start a three-to-ten-minute prefill that the caller will
abandon.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `local_admission_guard` evaluated **2 380** times: 1 965 `decision=admit
  reason=within_budget`, 415 `decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget`. The
  rejected ETAs had median **176 s** and max **876 s** against
  `budget_s=120.0`.
- The guard, per its own config comment, runs **before entering the contention
  queue** only ("Before entering the contention queue the proxy costs the
  projected local prefill … and compares it with the caller's wait budget").
  A request that finds a free slot is dispatched with no ETA ceiling.
- Result: **48 of 606** local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, and 91
  after >60 s (p50 8.9 s, p90 96.5 s, p99 443 s, max 592 s).
- llama-server prompt-eval durations confirm the cost: p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max
  591 s, at 77–302 t/s depending on size and contention.

So the guard already exists and is calibrated; it is simply bypassed on the
direct-dispatch path.

## Proposed change

1. Reuse the existing prefill-ETA estimator (observed `dispatch_first_byte_ms`,
   keyed by model + context bucket, rolling window — as used by
   LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) on the **direct dispatch** path, before the local
   request is sent upstream.
2. If projected prefill > the local wait budget, skip local and fall through to
   the next provider in the existing chain with an explicit log reason, e.g.
   `local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`.
3. Keep exactly one budget source (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, lowered
   to 60 s by the sibling child); do not add a second knob.
4. Keep the queue-entry guard unchanged — this is the same decision applied one
   step earlier.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A request whose projected prefill exceeds the budget is **never** dispatched
   locally, including when a local slot is free (unit test with a stubbed
   estimator).
2. A request whose projected prefill fits the budget is still dispatched locally
   on a free slot (no regression for the common case).
3. Behaviour is identical to today when the estimator has no samples yet
   (cold start): document the conservative default and cover it with a test.
4. Refusals are observable: log line with the projected ETA, the budget, and the
   chosen fallback provider; counter available on
   `/llama/local/status` if cheap to add.
5. Docs updated (routing/prefill section) and the config comment that claims the
   guard is queue-entry-only is corrected.
6. ≥24 h deployed measurement: local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` > budget ≈ 0
   (baseline 48), p99 ≤ 120 s; record numbers on the item.
7. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- **Estimator quality:** the ETA model is empirical; a mis-estimate either
  refuses work the box could have finished (lost local capacity) or admits a
  slow prefill (tail returns). Log projected vs observed so the estimator can be
  recalibrated, and keep the safety net of the prefill deadline child.
- **Cold start / new session shapes:** a session with a large but unusual prompt
  may project badly; the estimator's per-context-bucket history is the guard.
- **Load shifting:** refusals push work to rate-limited remotes — watch 429s.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (queue-entry implementation
  this extends).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation.
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement methodology.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: Prefill-ETA guard on direct (free-slot) local dispatch

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a live upstream stream **never** to lose its dispatch
lease or its slot to orphan cleanup, and when a stream is genuinely dead I want
its llama-server slot actually freed — so the proxy never dispatches new work
onto a GPU that is still busy, and its capacity accounting stays honest.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- **298** `lease_released ... reason=orphan_cleanup stream_abandoned=True`
  events vs only **6** `lease_verified_active ... stream_abandoned=False`
  extensions; i.e. the liveness verification almost never saves a lease.
- Of 118 local streams longer than 60 s, **81** had an `orphan_cleanup` inside
  their span, and the stream then went on to log `Stream finished` between 12 s
  and ~8 min later — the slot was declared dead while it was still working.
- `_query_slot_processing` (proxy/router_helpers.py) queries llama-server
  `/slots` with `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` default **1.0 s** and returns
  "not alive" (fail-open) on timeout or unverifiable response. Under a heavy
  prefill the llama-server event loop is busy and the query times out: the
  startup and earlier windows show `TimeoutError` from `_fetch_slots_payload`
  in observability.
- Prior work established that `/slots` is exactly the wrong signal during
  long prefills: LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC (`/slots` unobservable during long
  prefills), LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 (progress unobservable under load), and
  LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8 (watchdog released the lease but never cancelled the
  upstream prefill). This item closes the remaining hole: the **orphan path**
  still frees the lease/slot without cancelling the upstream stream (`stream_cm`
  is only captured and cancelled on the no-progress-watchdog path).
- Consequence of the bug: `local_active_queries` is decremented and the slot
  registry entry freed for work still running, so the admission guard and
  serialisation gate see a free GPU and admit new long prefills on top of a busy
  one — compounding the tail (1 827 `saturation=prefill` samples).

## Proposed change

1. **Fail-closed on unverifiable liveness during prefill:** mark the record
   "alive" when the `/slots` probe fails or times out and the prefill/generation
   progress signals are inconclusive, instead of destroying the orphan. Use the
   authoritative progress signals (prefill progress / chunk-refresh /
   no-progress watchdog — the same sources the lease-extension loop uses) as the
   primary liveness evidence.
2. If `/slots` is still probed, raise the timeout proportionally to context size
   (a 1 s probe against a busy 262 k slot is meaningless) or drop it for the
   prefill phase.
3. **When an orphan cleanup is genuinely applied** (no-progress watchdog
   confirmed nothing is moving), capture and cancel the upstream stream context
   (`stream_cm.__aexit__`) so the llama-server slot is actually released — the
   no-progress path already does this; extend the same to the orphan path.
4. Keep `local_active_queries` and the slot registry consistent with the cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A stream that later finishes is **never** orphan-cleaned in between
   (regression test replaying a long-prefill trace; counted as 0 of any sample).
2. `/slots` probe timeout or failure → treated as alive (extend), not as dead
   (unit test).
3. A genuinely wedged record (no progress) is still cleaned up, and its upstream
   stream is cancelled so the llama-server slot frees (unit test asserting the
   `stream_cm.__aexit__` path).
4. `local_active_queries` / slot registry stay consistent with actual upstream
   liveness (asserted in tests).
5. Docs updated (dispatch-lease / orphan-cleanup section of `docs/`) with the
   fail-closed rule.
6. ≥24 h measurement: `orphan_cleanup` ≤ 5 % of local dispatches (baseline 298
   ≈ 49 % of 606) and 0 orphan-cleaned streams that later finish (baseline 81);
   `lease_verified_active` no longer near-zero. Record numbers on the item.
7. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- A genuinely wedged slot keeps its lease longer if the "alive" default is too
  generous; the no-progress watchdog bound
  (`local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`) is the mitigation and must stay intact.
- Changing liveness verdicts alters capacity accounting; the measurement (AC6)
  is the gate before declaring the fix effective.

## Related work

- LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — `/slots` unobservable during long prefills (root cause
  of the probe failures).
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 — progress unobservable under load.
- LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8 — no-progress watchdog never cancelled upstream.
- LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2 — active-stream verification added to orphan cleanup
  (the flawed fail-open probe this corrects).
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: Fix orphan cleanup: fail-closed liveness, cancel upstream on true orphan

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the local model's prefill to run faster, so every local
first byte — and therefore the whole prefill-dominated tail — shrinks without
changing routing, admission or the GPU's other consumers.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- Current launch args for Qwen3 (from `models.ini` → start-llama.sh →
  llama-server): `--ubatch-size 1024`, `--batch-size 8192`, `--ctx-size 262144`,
  `--parallel 2`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `--flash-attn`.
- Measured prompt-eval throughput: p10 **77 t/s**, p50 211 t/s (20 k+ token
  batches), p90 **302 t/s**; prompt-eval durations p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max
  591 s.
- Sessions reach 170 k+ tokens (`routing_check estimated_tokens=174617`), and
  the proxy always re-sends the full prompt (`force_full_prompt: true` on the
  local-routed models), so llama-server must prefill large tails every turn;
  prefill is effectively the whole local response time (`dispatch_to_first_byte`
  ≈ total).
- Modern ggml prefill scales with ubatch size up to the GPU's compute/memory
  limits; 1024 is conservative for a 120 GB GPU with batch 8192.

## Proposed change

- `models.ini` `[Qwen3]`: `ubatch-size = 1024 → 2048`. (The operator wrote
  "2058"; that is not a meaningful value — this item interprets it as the
  power-of-two **2048**. Confirm on implementation; if 2058 was genuinely
  intended, correct the item.)
- **No TTS isolation**: TTS remains on the shared GPU; explicitly out of scope.
- No routing, admission or slot-pool changes in this item.
- llama-server restart required; the restart empties the prompt cache, so
  sequence the measurement window accordingly (cold bias for ~an hour).
- Verify with the existing benchmark harness before committing to the value
  (logs/proxy-benchmark.log, benchmark-results/, benchmark-qwen3*-*.json) and
  keep a documented revert (1024).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ubatch-size` is 2048 in `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with a comment recording the
   baseline (1024) and this item's measurement.
2. Benchmark A/B (same harness and workload as `benchmark-results/`): prompt-eval
   throughput (t/s) improves by **≥ 1.3×** at p90, or the change is reverted and
   the result recorded.
3. Decode throughput does not regress beyond noise (±2 %); VRAM stays within
   budget (no OOM; confirmed via llama-server startup + `rocm-smi`/monitoring).
4. ≥24 h post-change measurement via the proxy-usage-analysis CLI: local
   `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 and prompt-eval durations improve vs the
   baseline recorded above; numbers committed to the item.
5. Full test suite green (no code change expected — config only); commit + hash
   recorded.

## Risks

- **Cold-cache contamination:** the restart wipes the llama-server prompt cache
  (40 GiB) — first-byte stats will be inflated for the first hours. Take the
  measurement window after the cache warms, and note the restart in the item;
  do not compare cold first-day numbers with the baseline.
- **VRAM:** a larger ubatch raises peak activation memory. The benchmark gate
  (AC2) plus a memory check covers this.
- **Throughput may be memory-bandwidth bound already on this GPU** (Qwen3.6-35B
  is a hybrid MoE); if so the gain will be small — AC2 is the fail gate.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement methodology to reuse.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
