# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a short local turn never to be parked behind a giant
prefill, and a stalled prefill to surface as a fast detour rather than a silent
multi-minute hang — so the local tail is bounded by policy, not by whatever
happens to be first in the queue.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` (LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ) serialises prefills
  for good reason — measured 2026-10-19→20: first-byte p50 **23.4 s** alone vs
  **85.0 s** with one overlap, at **flat** aggregate throughput (~254 t/s). But
  it also means one long prefill is head-of-line blocking for every queued local
  request.
- `contention_queue_wait ... saturation=` shows **1 827** prefill-saturated
  samples vs 468 generating: the pool spends most of its life with one prefill
  blocking the other.
- `lease_extended_during_prefill` fired 6 685 times in the window — prefills
  routinely outlive the lease, and `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold` fired 450
  times across 119 sessions (first line of each: `waited=30s progress=0`).
- **48 of 606** local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, five after
  >400 s; the client sees a silent socket for that entire period (no SSE
  heartbeat during prefill), so it cannot distinguish "working" from "hung".
- `prefill_progress_unobservable` logged 1 242 times: the proxy itself often
  cannot say how far a prefill has got.

## Proposed change

Three coordinated behaviours (all previously recommended, none present today):

1. **ETA-aware admission ordering.** Among requests that are admissible
   locally, admit the smallest projected prefill first (shortest-ETA-first)
   instead of FIFO, so a 7-minute prefill cannot park a queue of 20-second
   turns. Lease-owner retention stays the primary tie-break so a returning
   warm-cache session is not starved; ordering applies within each retention
   class.
2. **Prefill heartbeat.** Emit SSE comment/keep-alive frames during prefill
   (e.g. `: prefill 42%` or a bare `: keep-alive` on a ≤30 s cadence, driven by
   the existing progress signal) so clients see liveness and their own
   first-byte timeouts are meaningful.
3. **Prefill deadline with automatic detour.** Add a configurable
   `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (default ~90). If the first byte has not
   arrived by then, cancel the local dispatch and fall through to the next
   provider, with a log reason and telemetry. This is the hard backstop
   independent of ETA-estimator quality; it must not fire for requests admitted
   legitimately inside their budget, so it is set well above the budget.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Ordering: a queued short-prefill request is not admitted after a long one
   when both are pending and both fit the budget (unit test with synthetic
   ETAs); retention priority still wins over size (unit test).
2. Heartbeat: during a local prefill longer than the cadence, SSE keep-alive
   frames are emitted at the configured cadence, and they stop when the first
   byte arrives (test asserting frame sequence and no leakage into the body).
3. Deadline: a dispatch with no first byte by the deadline is cancelled, the
   upstream request aborted, and the request routed to the next provider
   (test with a stalled upstream stub); no orphaned lease or slot is left behind
   (interacts with the orphan-cleanup child).
4. All three governed by documented config knobs with validation (malformed →
   safe default), no change to `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` semantics
   (single budget source).
5. ≥24 h measurement: local p99 first byte bounded by the deadline + margin
   (baseline 443 s, max 592 s); longest client-visible silent window ≤ the
   heartbeat cadence; no increase in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`
   per request. Record numbers on the item.
6. Docs updated (routing/prefill + streaming sections); full test suite green;
   commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- **Ordering can starve long prefills** under a stream of short ones. Retention
  wins first, and a long request that keeps losing should still get its budget
  (age-based promotion after N rejections or when its projected ETA still fits).
  Cover with a test.
- **Heartbeat frames** must be valid SSE comments for every client in use
  (pi/opencode/curl) and must not be counted as content by token accounting.
- **Deadline vs adaptive timeout:** the proxy already has an adaptive whole-
  request timeout and a session guardrail; the new deadline must be strictly
  shorter and must not conflict (document precedence).
- This child is the largest in the epic; if schedule pressure hits, ship in this
  order: deadline (safety) → heartbeat (UX) → ordering (scheduling).

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (the gate this schedules around).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA estimator to reuse.
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 / LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — progress-observability limits the
  heartbeat and deadline depend on.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: ETA-aware local admission + prefill heartbeat + prefill deadline

## Goal (user story)

As an operator watching the proxy Web UI, I want the `/events` SSE stream to
always deliver status updates (or at worst the 30 s keepalive) so that the UI
never appears frozen. Today a single cancelled `/slots` fetch can orphan a
shared single-flight future, after which affected SSE connections — and
potentially the whole periodic broadcast loop — hang forever and the UI stops
responding until the proxy is restarted.

## Reported symptom (2026-10-22)

"The proxy Web UI is not responding."

The proxy process was healthy and every non-SSE endpoint answered promptly:

```
GET /              200  0.005s
GET /health        200  0.022s
GET /v1/models     200  0.001s
GET /admin/sessions 200 0.001s
```

A *fresh* `GET /events` connection worked (first payload in ~0.5 s, then a
status event every ~1 s). The user's already-open tab received nothing at all —
not even the 30 s keepalive — while the TCP connection remained established, so
the browser's `EventSource` never reconnected and never errored. Hence
"not responding" with no visible failure.

## Verified root cause

`_fetch_slots_payload()` in `proxy/proxy/observability.py:296` (single-flight
coalescing for `/slots`, introduced by LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT):

```python
if not leader:
    return await fut                     # no timeout: waits forever
...
except Exception as exc:                 # CancelledError is BaseException - NOT caught
    if not fut.done():
        fut.set_exception(exc)
    raise
finally:
    async with lock:
        _slots_poll_inflight.pop(url, None)   # owner forgotten, future left PENDING
```

1. One caller (the "leader") performs the upstream `/slots` fetch; concurrent
   callers ("followers") `await fut`.
2. When a browser tab closes, reloads or navigates away, Starlette 1.0's
   `StreamingResponse` raises `ClientDisconnect` and cancels the handler task
   while it awaits the 5 s `/slots` fetch. The leader therefore exits via
   `asyncio.CancelledError`.
3. `asyncio.CancelledError` derives from `BaseException`, so `except Exception`
   does not run and `fut.set_exception()` is never called. The `finally` block
   removes the inflight entry, leaving the future **pending with nothing able
   to resolve it**.
4. Every follower already blocked on `await fut` hangs forever, because the
   follower wait has no timeout.
5. In `ui.status_events()` that await happens *before* the `while` loop that
   emits keepalives, so the generator yields zero bytes and the stream is
   silently dead. If `_periodic_broadcast_loop()`
   (`observability.py:1737`) takes the follower path, the loop that drives
   updates for **all** connected clients stalls permanently.

### Reproduction (real code path, `_do_slots_fetch` stubbed with a slow fetch)

```
leader cancelled (client disconnected)
REPRODUCED: follower still hanging after 3s -> orphaned future, no timeout on `await fut`
inflight entries left: []
```

### Why it triggers frequently

The local Qwen3 child serialises `/slots` behind inference. Measured during
generation: `:50193/slots?model=Qwen3` took **23.7 s** versus 0.5 ms idle — 4.7x
the 5 s timeout used by `_query_slots_detail`. While the model is busy, every
slots query times out, giving a wide window in which any disconnect cancels a
leader. Evidence from `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`:

- 582 `TimeoutError`s from `_query_slots_detail`
- recurring `status_request ... latency_ms=2000..5500 ... slots_stale=true`
- `client_disconnect reaped in-flight request task=Task-118472` style entries

## Scope

1. `_fetch_slots_payload()`: handle `asyncio.CancelledError` (and any
   `BaseException`) by cancelling/resolving the shared future before
   re-raising, so followers are never left waiting on a future nobody owns.
2. `_fetch_slots_payload()`: bound the follower wait and degrade gracefully
   (retry as a new leader, or fall back to the last-known payload) on timeout,
   so a dead owner can never hang a caller indefinitely.
3. `ui.status_events()`: bound the initial `query_llama_status()` await (it is
   currently unbounded) so no single backend call can hold an SSE stream open
   without ever emitting a keepalive.
4. Regression tests in `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py` covering the
   cancellation paths (not covered today — all 8 existing tests are
   happy-path/TTL/backoff only).

Out of scope: the underlying `/slots` blocking behaviour on the llama-server
child (upstream, and tracked separately by the existing slots-staleness items);
the frontend is not changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A follower awaiting an in-flight `/slots` fetch is released when the leader is cancelled (`asyncio.CancelledError`), rather than blocking forever; a regression test asserts the follower completes within a bounded time and that the inflight registry is empty afterwards.
- AC2: A follower never waits unboundedly — if the leader disappears without resolving the future, the follower either re-fetches as a new leader or returns the last-known/cached values within its own timeout.
- AC3: Cancelling a request that owns the single-flight fetch does not leak a pending future or emit "Future exception was never retrieved" / "Task was destroyed but it is pending" warnings.
- AC4: `status_events()` emits its initial payload or a keepalive within a bounded time even when `query_llama_status()` is slow or degraded.
- AC5: Documented reproduction fails before the fix and passes after it, using the existing test-skill runner (no ad-hoc pytest invocations).

## Related

- LP-0MUCEFD5B003TURT — "Throttle and coalesce /slots status polling under
  local load" (introduced the single-flight helper; also recorded the
  4554 cancel-task warnings adjacent to `GET /slots` on the llama-server child,
  which is consistent with this cancellation path).
- LP-0MVECWYWK000U3E1 — "Slot status serves stale log-derived progress, so the
  Web UI shows slots frozen" (same symptom surface: frozen Web UI).
- LP-0MRWQCEG700364G9 — "Web UI slot status shows stale token counts when
  /slots API times out".


## Key Files (predicted, verified against current source)

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:295` — `_fetch_slots_payload()`: fix `asyncio.CancelledError`/`BaseException` handling so the shared future is always resolved; bound the follower `await fut` with a timeout and degrade gracefully (re-fetch as leader or return last-known payload).
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:1737` — `_periodic_broadcast_loop()`: the follower stall path that can hang the broadcast loop for **all** connected clients.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py:347` — `status_events()`: bound the initial `query_llama_status()` await (currently unbounded) so the SSE stream always emits its first payload or a keepalive.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py` — add regression tests for the leader-cancellation / orphaned-future paths (existing 8 tests are happy-path/TTL/backoff only).
data.title: Proxy Web UI /events stream hangs forever when a /slots single-flight leader is cancelled

# Prefill parsing and matching tests

## Summary

Create test fixtures and unit tests for the prefill time analysis: `dispatch_first_byte_ms` parsing per local request, TTFT→stream matching by session (FIFO), and boundary conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fixtures copied from real `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` lines carrying `dispatch_first_byte_ms=` (warm and cold cache states, non-zero `queue_wait_ms`, and aborted streams with no `dispatch_first_byte_ms`) are added to `tests/fixtures.py`.
- The prefill parser tests cover `dispatch_first_byte_ms` extraction: `log_parser.parse_log_line()` yields `kind=ttft` with `ttft_ms`, plus `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms`, `queue_wait_ms`, `cache_state`, `cached_ratio`, `session` and `model`, matching the real-line format exactly.
- TTFT→stream matching tests cover the prefill parser's FIFO pairing: for each session the Nth `dispatch_first_byte_ms` event pairs with the Nth `stream_started` event by timestamp, across single- and multi-request sessions.
- Unit tests cover the union-interval busy calculation's inputs: streams with no `dispatch_first_byte_ms` (aborted streams) are reported as "unknown prefill" rather than silently dropped.
- Tests cover the fast/cheap split fixtures on the new intervals: the same session events bucket identically whether the interval starts at `Stream started` or at the back-calculated dispatch time.
- Tests cover the empty-eval-timing diagnostic path fixture: a llama-server log file with no eval-timing lines and one with an undiscoverable Qwen3 port both parse without error and report zero samples.
- Unit tests cover: the prefill parser, the union-interval busy calculation (including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams), the fast/cheap split on the new intervals, and the empty-eval-timing diagnostic path, with fixtures copied from real `/var/log/llama-proxy` lines (`dispatch_first_byte_ms=`).

## Key Files

- `tests/fixtures.py`
- `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

None (foundation test fixtures).

# Prefill interval model & statistics aggregation

## Summary

Extend `aggregation.py` to compute per-local-stream prefill seconds from `dispatch_first_byte_ms` TTFT events, including p10/p50/p90/max and window total. Define the prefill interval as `[dispatch_ts, first_byte_ts]` where `dispatch_ts = ttft_event.ts - dispatch_first_byte_ms/1000` and `first_byte_ts = ttft_event.ts`. Add `prefill_stats` to `BusyStats` with a statement that figures are slot-seconds, not wall-clock.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `compute_busy_stats()` in `aggregation.py` accepts the local TTFT events, pairs them to streams per session (FIFO by timestamp), and computes and reports **local prefill time** **per local stream** from `dispatch_first_byte_ms`.
- The prefill figure falls back to pairing the dispatch and first-byte timestamps when `dispatch_first_byte_ms` is absent, and the fallback is documented in the function docstring.
- `BusyStats.prefill_stats` reports **p10/p50/p90/max** and the **window total** prefill, with an explicit statement that the figure is **slot-time, not wall-clock**.
- The prefill interval is `[ttft_event.ts - ttft_ms/1000, ttft_event.ts]`; streams without a TTFT event are counted as unknown prefill and excluded from percentiles but retained in the total count.
- The window total prefill is the sum of per-stream prefill durations (total prefill work), explicitly distinguished from the wall-clock union used for busy time.
- Unit tests verify prefill matching, percentile computation, unknown-prefill handling, and boundary conditions (dispatch before `window_start`, TTFT after `window_end`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/aggregation.py`
- `scripts/log_parser.py`
- `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- LP-0MVJN025B001I8AL (test fixtures)

# Union-interval busy redefinition (dispatch → finish)

## Summary

Redefine `Local model utilization` busy time as the union of `dispatch → finish` intervals (prefill + decode), retaining the decode-only figure as a separate row. Label lower/upper bounds. Keep existing fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats working on the new intervals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Local model utilization` reports `busy` as the **union of dispatch → finish intervals** (prefill + decode), using `ttft_event.ts - ttft_ms/1000` as the interval start.
- The **decode-only figure is retained alongside as a separate row** (`decode_busy_seconds`, the union of `Stream started` → `Stream finished`), and the report carries a **labelled lower/upper bound** for the busy figure.
- The busy definition change is stated explicitly in the section header: busy = at least one local slot active from dispatch to finish (prefill + decode).
- Existing **fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats keep working on the new intervals**: `fast_busy_seconds`, `cheap_busy_seconds`, `hourly_busy`, `avg_concurrency`, `peak_concurrency` and `total_compute_seconds` are all recomputed on dispatch→finish.
- Streams without a TTFT event fall back to `[stream_started_ts, finish_ts]` and are attributed to the lower bound, so the busy figure is never overstated.
- Unit tests verify the union of dispatch→finish intervals including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams, that the decode-only figure is retained, and that overlapping prefill+decode intervals merge correctly.

## Key Files

- `scripts/aggregation.py`
- `scripts/reporting.py`
- `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- LP-0MVJN45LF009CO2V (prefill interval model)
data.title: Redefine local busy as dispatch-to-finish union

# Goal (user story)

As an operator/agent, I want the client to receive SSE keep-alive frames
while a local request is still in its **strict prefill window** (before the
upstream first byte), so a long prefill is visibly alive instead of a silent
socket that the client cannot distinguish from a hang.

Discovered during LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6 (epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD): the item's
AC2 asks for keep-alive frames during prefill "and they stop when the first
byte arrives", but the existing `stream_heartbeat_interval_seconds` (default
10 s, `data: {"type":"heartbeat",...}`) only flows **after** the upstream
SSE headers arrive. For this llama.cpp build the headers arrive with the
first token, so the strict prefill window (the dominant tail: baseline 48 of
606 local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, max 592 s) is completely
silent to the client.

## Why it was split out

`proxy_to_local` awaits `_await_first_byte_with_prefill_monitor` **before**
constructing the `StreamingResponse`, so no bytes can reach the client until
the upstream first byte. Emitting frames earlier needs the local dispatch to
return a streaming response *first* and move the first-byte wait into the
generator — a restructure of a large, delicate function that owns the lease
and slot lifecycle. Doing it under schedule pressure in the parent item would
have risked the tail it is meant to fix.

## Proposed change

1. For streaming requests, return a `StreamingResponse` immediately on the
   local path and perform the first-byte wait inside the generator, so
   keep-alive frames can be written while waiting.
2. Emit SSE comment frames (`: keep-alive` or `: prefill <pct>`) on a
   configurable cadence (reuse/clarify `stream_heartbeat_interval_seconds`
   or add `local_prefill_heartbeat_seconds`), stopping as soon as the first
   byte is forwarded.
3. Frames must be valid SSE comments for pi/opencode/curl and must not be
   counted as content by token accounting or by the content-delivered
   re-route boundary in `_preflight_streaming_response`.
4. Leases: the moved wait must keep the existing prefill-lease extension,
   the prefill deadline (LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6) and the fail-closed orphan rule
   (LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0) intact.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A local prefill longer than the cadence emits keep-alive frames at the
   configured cadence **before** the upstream first byte (test asserting the
   frame sequence with a stalled-upstream stub).
2. Frames stop when the first byte arrives and never leak into the response
   body/token accounting (test asserting no frame appears after content).
3. The content-delivered re-route boundary is unaffected (no pre-content
   frame may suppress recovery re-routing).
4. Lease/slot accounting and the prefill deadline still behave as tested in
   LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6 / LP-0MVIQ0FJC000YLX0.
5. Malformed cadence config falls back to a safe default; docs updated.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIQ0G2M0006QF6 — parent (deadline + ordering landed; this is its AC2).
- LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — epic.
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 / LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — prefill observability limits.
data.title: Emit SSE heartbeat frames during the strict prefill window (before upstream first byte)

# Goal (bug)

As an operator, I want a change to `models.ini` or `start-llama.sh` (model launch arguments: `ubatch-size`, `batch-size`, `ctx-size`, cache types, …) to force a llama-server restart on `start-proxy.sh --restart`, so a config edit is never silently left inactive.

## Evidence (2026-10-22, LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS)

Setting `ubatch-size = 2048` in `models.ini` [Qwen3] and `UBATCH_SIZE=2048` / `LLAMA_UBATCH_SIZE:=2048` in `start-llama.sh`, then running `scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart`, left llama-server running with `--ubatch-size 1024`. Cause: the preserve decision hashes only the merged `config.yaml`

```
_restart_sha=$(merged_config_sha256(config.yaml, <overlay>))
# compared with .llama_server_signature.json config_sha256
if [ "$_sig_sha" = "$_restart_sha" ]; then KEEP_LLAMA=1; fi
```

`models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` are the actual launch-argument sources (the startup log even prints `BATCH_SIZE=…`), but they are not part of the signature, so any edit to them is invisible to the restart decision.

Workaround used at the time: delete `proxy/.llama_server_signature.json` to force `KEEP_LLAMA=0`. That is undocumented and easy to get wrong (the file lives under `proxy/`, not the repo root, although the script computes `REPO_ROOT` as the parent of `proxy/`).

## Proposed change

1. Include the model-launch inputs in the restart signature: hash `models.ini` and `start-llama.sh` (and any other launch-argument source the script reads) alongside the merged config.
2. Surface the reason in the startup log, e.g. `Restarting llama-server: models.ini changed since last start`, next to the existing preserve message.
3. Document the forced-restart escape hatch (`--force-llama-server` flag or removing the signature file) in the start-proxy skill and README.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Editing `models.ini` (e.g. a comment-only change and a value change, tested separately) followed by `start-proxy.sh --restart` restarts llama-server (test or documented manual verification with the observed argv).
2. Editing `start-llama.sh` likewise restarts llama-server.
3. An unchanged config/models.ini/start-llama.sh trio still preserves the warm llama-server (no regression to LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN).
4. The startup log names which input changed.
5. The forced-restart path is documented in the start-proxy skill and `proxy/README.md`.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIQ0FSX006HQOS — the ubatch A/B where this was hit (reverted; commit c9a49039).
- LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN — the original "preserve the warm llama-server on a proxy-only restart" decision this must not regress.
- LP-0MVAPNC2900145RH — restart-reason plumbing in the same script.

# Intake brief: run the idle-admission measurement window

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-aware local admission override enabled for one
full ≥24 h window and analysed with `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, so
LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD's AC1–AC5 can be resolved (enable by default, or record
the tuning) with measured numbers instead of a counterfactual estimate.

## Why this is a separate item

LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD landed the measurement tooling (commit `c99ac884`):
`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, the `priority=`/`estimated_tokens=` dispatch
fields, `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` and the config documentation.
What it cannot do is satisfy its own ACs, because the override is **off by
default** (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled: false`) and zero
`routing_idle_admit` events exist in any logged window. Enabling it changes live
routing, and the 24 h window cannot elapse inside a session — hence this item.

## Steps

1. Decide whether to enable the override for the window (live routing change:
   idle GPU time is spent on economic bypasses instead of paid remote calls,
   at the risk of a long first byte on an idle-admitted 120 K prompt).
2. Set `server.local_idle_admit_enabled: true` (keep
   `server.local_idle_admit_seconds: 60` for the first window), restart the
   proxy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, and record the restart timestamp.
3. Wait ≥ 24 h (the window cannot be shortened).
4. Run:
   `python3 scripts/idle_admit_impact.py --before-start '<baseline 24 h>' --before-end '<...>' --after-start '<restart>' --after-end '<+24 h>' --deployed-at '<restart>' --window-closed --json > /tmp/idle_admit_24h.json`
   plus `--markdown` for the report section.
5. Record the numbers + verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD, then apply the AC5
   recommendation: keep the flag on (`enable_by_default`), or open the tuning
   follow-up the tool proposes and set the flag accordingly.

## Notes

- The baseline of record is 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 (table in the
  parent item and in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`).
- The counterfactual estimate over 2026-10-21 19:00 → 2026-10-22 19:00 was 937
  of 1,235 economic bypasses (75.9 %) with ≥ 60 s of system-wide local idle —
  the expected size of the win, not a measurement.
- Batch with LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (restored-prefix warmness, also waiting on a
  24 h post-deploy window) to avoid two separate experimental windows.
- `proxy-usage-analysis` reports the same override from the other side; use its
  05:00 daily report as the AC1 artifact of record when convenient.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The override has run for ≥ 24 h with `local_idle_admit` events > 0, and the
   window start is recorded (post-restart).
2. `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py --window-closed` runs clean on the window and
   its JSON artifact is attached to LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.
3. The AC1–AC4 numbers are recorded on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the
   2026-10-19/20 baseline.
4. The AC5 outcome is decided and recorded: either `enable_by_default` (flag
   stays on) or the tuning follow-up (threshold / prompt-size cap / priority
   gating) is filed with the measured evidence.


## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# Instrument and fix the slot sidecar seed path (restored-prefix warmness never fires)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the restored-prefix credit (LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) to
actually fire for sessions that resume with a persisted slot snapshot, so the
feature is measurable — and if it cannot fire for the common case, I want to
know why with instrumentation instead of silence.

## Problem statement

The ≥24 h measurement (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K, 2026-10-22) found the seeding path
made **zero contact** in a 54.4 h post-deploy window:

- 0 `slot_ratio_restored` events, 0 `cache_state=restored` lines;
- the sidecar writer is healthy: 37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars
  written (2026-10-20 13:27 → 2026-10-22 19:43), names match the reader's
  candidate layout (`slot-cache/localhost-8080/`);
- 33 sessions with sidecars reached the local routing gate 2,918 times after
  their sidecar existed (including right after proxy restarts when the in-memory
  ratio was empty) and were still scored `cache_state=cold` — e.g. session
  `herdr-1792667491-…` (sidecar: 276 messages, saved 14:13) scored
  `cached_ratio=0.00 cache_state=cold messages=696` at 19:30 after a restart.

Root-cause suspects (in order of likelihood): (1) the `prefix_matches` guard
fails on real resumed conversations — first message (system prompt) regenerated
per request, and/or client-side compaction rewriting the front of the history
(proxy-side compaction is disabled: `compaction_bypass_eval … reason=compaction_disabled`);
(2) sidecars only exist for old snapshots, so a 24 h TTL plus front-rewrites
leaves no credit window; (3) (checked, unlikely) endpoint string drift between
save and seed. Seed outcomes log at DEBUG only, invisible at the INFO level the
proxy runs at.

## Split at producer request (2026-10-22)

The producer chose **instrument first**. The observability half is now its own S
child, **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** (INFO-level `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` logging +
tests + docs), and this item depends on it. Do not change the credit logic
(`prefix_matches`, the sidecar TTL, the sidecar format) until the interface has
produced one traffic cycle of outcome counts: a fix attempted without that data
is guesswork. Effort below (M) covers the remaining fix plus the ≥24 h
re-measurement; priority is medium while it waits on data.

## Proposed change

1. Using the instrumented outcome counts, decide which failure mode is real:
   too-strict `prefix_matches` (rewritten system prompt / client-compacted
   history), an expired sidecar (24 h TTL vs long-lived sessions), or a lookup
   miss. Record the decision and the supporting data on this item.
2. Fix only the confirmed cause, consistent with AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (a
   *changed* prompt still earns nothing; a *reusable prefix* must earn credit).
   Candidate approaches to evaluate: fingerprint the non-system messages only;
   anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash; credit the last-saved overlapping
   messages; or compare against the last K messages of the stored list instead
   of requiring a prefix. Re-evaluate the TTL if it is the binding constraint.
3. Add a unit test reproducing the real resume pattern (sidecar saved for a full
   conversation; resumed request arrives with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   compacted front) that fails before the fix and passes after it.
4. Re-run the ≥24 h before/after measurement with
   `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (built by LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K):
   post-fix `cache_state=restored` dispatches must be > 0, and seeded dispatches
   must beat cold dispatches in the same context bucket (sample counts +
   percentiles).
5. Document the changed guard in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A written verdict on this item names the confirmed failure mode and cites the instrumented outcome counts that prove it.
- For the confirmed cause, a unit test reproduces the resume-with-rewritten-front case and fails on the pre-fix code.
- After the fix, a ≥24 h window contains `cache_state=restored` dispatches, and their `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles are stated against cold dispatches in the same context bucket with sample counts.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (mismatched snapshots earn nothing; restored ratio ≤ measured × margin).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the resolved guard and its failure modes.

## Risks / notes

- The 24 h TTL (`session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds`) may itself be too short for
  the resume pattern observed (sidecar at 276 messages, resume at 696); include
  TTL in the investigation.
- Attribution caveat: the local-prefill improvement in the measurement window
  came from other changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering); do not
  use it as evidence for this path.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (the AC5 measurement that found zero seeds)
- implementation of: LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (restored slot-prefix warmness)
- blocked by: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (seed-outcome instrumentation)
- report: docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — the seed path and its guard: `prefix_matches()`,
  `seed_cached_ratio()` (validation order: snapshot → sidecar → model → TTL → prefix),
  `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()`. The confirmed-cause fix lands here.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` applies the *same*
  `prefix_matches` guard to the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812); a guard change
  must be evaluated for both call sites, not just the sidecar.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — add the resume-with-rewritten-front
  reproducer alongside the existing guard/TTL tests.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530): document the
  resolved guard and its failure modes.
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — the AC3 re-measurement.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the baseline the
  re-measurement is compared against.

## Plan (features and implementation tasks, 2026-10-22)

The five acceptance criteria decompose into three independently deliverable
slices plus the prerequisite instrumentation, in dependency order (verification
slices before implementation, per the plan skill's test-first rule):

| # | Work item | Type | Covers | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** — Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO | task (S, risk Low) | prerequisite data (INFO `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`) | — |
| 1 | **LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3** — Diagnose the seed failure mode from outcome counts | task (verification) | AC1 | item 0 |
| 2 | **LP-0MVK0E80C009HUQC** — Fix the confirmed seed guard and document it | bug (test-first slice) | AC2, AC4, AC5 | item 1 |
| 3 | **LP-0MVK0E8NH007XCV3** — Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix | task (verification) | AC3 | item 2 |

**Why three slices:** AC1 needs the instrumentation's outcome counts (a
traffic-cycle wait), and AC3 needs a ≥24 h post-fix window (another wait).
Neither wait can complete inside a single fix run, so each is its own item
with its own worktree lifecycle; the fix itself stays one vertical slice
(code + failing-then-passing test + docs) rather than being split
horizontally.

**Deliberately undecided:** the fix technique (non-system fingerprinting, a
stable prompt-prefix anchor, last-K overlap credit, or a TTL change) is chosen
from the diagnosis verdict, not here — the producer's "instrument first" split
stands. A fix attempted without the outcome counts is guesswork.

**Between phases:** after the diagnosis verdict lands, re-read the fix item's
description and update it so the reproducer test and the guard change match
the confirmed mode; after the fix lands, confirm the deployed build before the
re-measurement window starts.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7** – Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing) (open)
- **LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K** – Measure restored slot-prefix warmness impact over >=24h (before/after) (completed)
- **LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV** – Second-turn cached_ratio scored 0.00 after a successful cold first local turn (bootstrap defect in update_cached_ratio) (completed)

### Repository file matches (verified by inspection)
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — `prefix_matches()` (the suspected guard), `seed_cached_ratio()` validation order, `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()` (TTL), `_candidate_slot_filenames()` (lookup)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` reuses the same `prefix_matches` guard for the in-memory expected-reuse credit (~L812), so any guard change affects both paths; `_last_prompt_prefix` store
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — existing guard/TTL tests (`test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`, `test_expired_sidecar_earns_no_credit`, `test_ttl_zero_disables_expiry`) to extend with the resume-with-rewritten-front case
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530) to update
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — ≥24 h before/after re-measurement tool
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — baseline figures and sidecar inventory to compare against

## Intake notes (verification pass, 2026-10-22)

- **No interview required.** The seed brief already carried a problem statement with
  evidence, five measurable acceptance criteria, scoped constraints ("do not change the
  credit logic until the instrumentation has produced one traffic cycle"), risks and
  traceability; the remaining questions are answerable from the repo, which was read
  during this pass (seed path, guard, tests, docs, measurement report).
- **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search` on "slot sidecar restored prefix warmness"):
  no duplicate item exists. Related, non-overlapping items are the completed implementation
  LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304, the completed measurement LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (which triggered this
  item), the open instrumentation child LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and the completed
  expected-reuse credit LP-0MVI2XOTY008Q4UV.
- **Assumption (recorded, not decided):** the failure mode is not chosen here. The
  producer's "instrument first" split stands — this item stays `blocked` on
  LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 and its fix is selected from the instrumented outcome counts.
- **Note on the shared guard:** because `prefix_matches` is also used by
  `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` for the in-memory expected-reuse credit, any guard
  change is a two-call-site change; the AC2 unit test must therefore assert the sidecar
  path *and* confirm the expected-reuse path still refuses a genuinely changed prompt
  (AC4).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan, 2026-10-22)

**No operator questions were asked in this session.** Rationale: the intake
brief already carried the producer's "instrument first" decision, five
measurable ACs, explicit scope constraints and full traceability; the
plan-approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (effort Medium, risk
Medium — the gate pauses only for Extra Large effort combined with High/Severe
risk), so no approval pause was warranted. Everything the plan needed was
answerable from this work item and the repository, which was read during this
session.

**Decision log (agent-made, evidence-linked):**

- **D1 — decompose into three children** instead of implementing as one unit.
  Evidence: AC1 depends on a traffic cycle of instrumentation data and AC3 on
  a ≥24 h post-fix window; both are waits that cannot complete inside a fix
  run. Splitting lets each be worked, reviewed and closed on its own worktree
  lifecycle.
- **D2 — keep the reproducer test inside the fix item** (TDD slice), not in a
  separate child. Evidence: AC2 requires the test to fail on the *pre-fix*
  code, so a standalone red test cannot be delivered or closed independently;
  width comes from tests-plus-docs inside the slice instead.
- **D3 — converted the numbered AC lists to bullet form** (this item and its
  instrumentation child), text unchanged. Evidence: the shared tree-coverage
  review (`shared/tree_coverage.extract_acceptance_criteria`) reads `- `
  bullets only, so numbered ACs made the automated parent↔child coverage check
  report vacuously "fully covered". No requirement text was altered.
- **D4 — the fix technique stays open** until the diagnosis verdict names the
  failure mode; recorded on the fix item (its step 2) and on this item's
  "Proposed change" section.
- **D5 — the 24 h TTL is in scope only if the diagnosis proves it binding**;
  the fix item must then record the observed `age_s` distribution as the
  numerical justification.
- **D6 — instrumentation child advanced to `plan_complete`** via the plan
  skill's auto-complete path (effort S, risk Low): its existing ACs, proposed
  change and risks were reviewed, and a verified `## Key Files` section was

**Assumptions (recorded, not decided):** the instrumentation build reaches
production and serves one full traffic cycle; the confirmed cause stays inside
the documented seed path (guard, TTL, lookup); the guard change must be applied
at both `prefix_matches` call sites (sidecar seed and in-memory expected-reuse
credit).

**OPEN QUESTION:** none blocking. The one open *technical* question — which
guard semantics are correct — is intentionally deferred to the diagnosis

## Plan: changelog (2026-10-22)

# Instrument slot-sidecar seed outcomes at INFO (measure before fixing)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want every local routing decision that *could* have been
credited from a persisted slot snapshot to say what happened at INFO level, so
the restored-prefix feature's real failure mode (guard too strict, snapshot
missing/expired, or nothing reusable) is measurable from logs instead of
inferred — before anyone changes the credit logic.

## Why (evidence)

The ≥24 h measurement LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K found the seeding path made **zero
contact** in 54.4 h: 0 `slot_ratio_restored` events, 0 `cache_state=restored`
dispatches, while 37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars were written and
33 sidecar-bearing sessions hit the local routing gate **2,918** times after
their sidecar existed (including post-restart, e.g. session
`herdr-1792667491-…` scored `cached_ratio=0.00 cache_state=cold` with 696
messages against a 276-message sidecar). Today the only diagnostic
(`slot_ratio_sidecar skipped reason=prefix_mismatch …`) is DEBUG, and the proxy
runs at INFO — so the failure is unobservable. Any fix attempted now is
guesswork between (a) `prefix_matches` rejecting rewritten system prompts /
client-compacted history, (b) the 24 h sidecar TTL, and (c) an unexpected
lookup miss.

This item is the instrumentation step of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (the fix), split
off at producer request so the fix is decided from data.

## Scope

**In scope:** observability only — a new INFO log line (and reason vocabulary),
plus tests and docs. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit decision,
`prefix_matches`, TTL, the sidecar format, or `cached_ratio` scoring. The
instrumentation must be behaviour-neutral.

## Proposed change

1. In the seed path (`proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, called from
   `provider.py`), emit one INFO line per local routing decision when a
   candidate session *could* have a snapshot (i.e. at least one candidate
   `slot_<session>.bin` / sidecar file resolves, or a sidecar exists but the
   snapshot does not). Follow the existing single-line `key=value` logging
   style and reuse the short session id, e.g.:

   ```
   slot_ratio_seed outcome=<found|missing_snapshot|missing_sidecar|expired|model_mismatch|prefix_mismatch|empty_ratio> session=<8> model=Qwen3 stored_messages=<n> incoming_messages=<n> age_s=<n> cached_ratio=<x.xx>
   ```

   Decisions for sessions with no snapshot at all stay silent (the common
   case), so this cannot flood the log (upper bound ≈ current `routing_check`
   volume for snapshot-bearing sessions only).
2. Keep `slot_ratio_restored` as-is for a successful seed (the measurement
   tool and `LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC` key off it) and make the new line the
   complementary skip/outcome record.
3. Document the vocabulary and how to aggregate it in `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   (one short section), so the usage report can sum outcomes later without
   re-deriving them.
4. Tests: unit tests covering every outcome branch with a synthetic sidecar
   (found / expired / model mismatch / prefix mismatch / missing snapshot /
   missing sidecar), asserting the line is emitted at INFO with the expected
   `outcome=` value and message counts; a test asserting **no** line is emitted
   when the session has no snapshot (no flood, no behaviour change); a test
   asserting the credited ratio is unchanged (behaviour-neutral).

## Acceptance criteria

- A routing decision with a resolvable snapshot emits exactly one INFO
   `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` line carrying `session`, `model`,
   `stored_messages`, `incoming_messages`, `age_s`, and `outcome` from the
   documented vocabulary.
- All six outcomes are individually observable (each covered by a unit test);
   the current `prefix_mismatch` DEBUG line is superseded (no duplicated
   DEBUG/INFO pair for the same event).
- No line is emitted for sessions without a snapshot — verified by a test that
   asserts log output is unchanged for that case.

## Risks / notes

## Goal (user story)

As the operator running the N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep (LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD), I want a
fail-closed quiet-window preflight check plus validated harness commands, so the sweep is
never attempted against a proxy that other sessions are using — the exact failure mode that
aborted the 2026-10-20 attempt (every benchmark turn-1 request stalled at 600–760 s against
the 1200 s timeout, llama-server stopped answering health probes, config had to be restored).

## Context

- The 2026-10-20 attempt ran the sweep while 5 concurrent sessions (2 audits + 4 herdr panes)
  held local leases; the harness has no notion of "is the host quiet".
- `GET http://localhost:8000/llama/local/status` already exposes the needed signals:
  `local_owner_session_id`, `local_idle_seconds`, `available_slots` / `total_slots`,
  `llama_server_running`, and per-slot `lease_state` / `is_processing` / `phase`.
- The parent's commands are slightly off for their intent: `--sweep` is `[1, 2, 3]`, so N=1
  (out of scope, and already measured) must be skipped with `--resume 2`; N=4 is `--slots 4`.
- `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` is now **60** (halved from 120 by
  LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO), not 120 as the parent description states, so any queue-timeout
  rate must record the value in force to stay comparable with the 2026-10-17 sweep.
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` already restores the config on any failure, records
  `config_diff`, `system_memory_bytes`, `observed_slots` and viability warnings; this child
  adds only the missing *quiet* gate and command validation.

## Implementation sketch

- `scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py`: GET `/llama/local/status`, evaluate the quiet predicate,
  print a human verdict plus `--json` machine output, exit non-zero (fail closed) when not
  quiet or when the endpoint is unreachable.
- Quiet predicate: `llama_server_running is True` AND `local_owner_session_id is None` AND
  every slot has `lease_state == "free"` AND `is_processing is False` AND
  `available_slots == total_slots` AND `local_idle_seconds >= --min-idle-seconds` (default 120).
- Unit tests for the predicate and the exit codes.
- `--dry-run` validation of both harness command forms.

**Key Files:**
- scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py
- tests/test_slot_sweep_preflight.py
- proxy/benchmarks/README.md
- proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `python3 scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py` exits 0 only when the status payload reports
   `llama_server_running == true`, `local_owner_session_id is null`, every slot
   `lease_state == "free"` and `is_processing == false`,
   `available_slots == total_slots`, and `local_idle_seconds >= --min-idle-seconds`
   (default 120); otherwise it exits non-zero and prints the specific failing clause.
2. `--json` output carries the evaluated predicate inputs and a machine-readable
   `quiet: true|false` plus `reasons[]`; an unreachable `/llama/local/status` (or a
   non-200 response) exits non-zero with `quiet: false`.
3. Unit tests cover: the quiet pass; a leased slot; `is_processing` true; a
   `available_slots != total_slots` mismatch; idle below threshold; `llama_server_running`
   false; endpoint unreachable. Removing any single clause of the predicate makes at least
   one test fail.
4. `python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark --sweep --resume 2 --concurrency 3
   --prompt-tokens 2000 --dry-run` exits 0 and shows the run list `2, 3` (no N=1), and
   `... --slots 4 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 --dry-run` exits 0 for `4`.
5. `sha256sum proxy/config.yaml` is identical before and after the preflight plus both dry
   runs — no config write before the measured sweep starts.
6. A comment on LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD records: the validated command set (including the
   `--resume 2` correction), `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` in force, and the N=4
   memory gate adopted by the run child.
7. `proxy/benchmarks/README.md` documents the preflight step for the slot sweep.

## Notes / assumptions

- Default idle window 120 s is the documented assumption (a lease can idle briefly between
  turns); it is a CLI flag so the run child can tighten it.
- No production routing behaviour changes — this is an operator tool plus tests.

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the controlled N=2 (baseline), N=3 and — memory permitting — N=4
slot sweep executed in a verified quiet window with its results committed, so the
concurrency-vs-capacity projection in
`docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (N=2 denies ~19.7% of session-minutes,
N=3 ~6.7%, N=4 ~2.2%) is validated or refuted against real local TTFT, decode speed,
queue-timeout rate and memory.

## Context

- Parent AC1/AC2. Predecessor: the preflight/validation child (blocking).
- Prior attempt (2026-10-20) is invalid: local leases starved the benchmark, all turn-1
  requests stalled, llama-server stopped answering health probes. The 2026-10-17 sweep
  (LP-0MVAZPQUM006EAC7) is also invalid for local metrics (`local share 0.0%` — everything
  fell back remote) but its queue-timeout rates are valid.
- So this run is only meaningful if the benchmark requests actually land on the local
  backend: **local stream share must be > 0**, otherwise the run is recorded as
  INVALID and the child stops rather than producing a misleading verdict.
- Memory is not expected to bind at N=4: per `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py`, total
  KV is constant (~2.7 GiB) and model+KV ≈ 27.4 GiB at every slot count, so the cost of N=4
  is the per-slot context clamp (61,440) and warm-threshold shrink (58,368), not VRAM.
- `--sweep` is `[1, 2, 3]`; use `--resume 2`. `generate_report()` rewrites
  `slot_benchmark_report.json` / `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` on every invocation, so the
  N=4 invocation must not overwrite the N=2/N=3 report.

## Procedure (single quiet window, one session)

1. Run the preflight gate until it passes (`scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py`); record its
   JSON output in the results note. Do not start the sweep unless it exits 0.
2. Record the environment: `sha256sum proxy/config.yaml`, `session_slot_pool_size`,
   `local_model_ctx_size`, `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`,
   `local_max_concurrent_prefills`, system MemAvailable, and any other lease holders.
3. `LLAMA_PROXY_BENCHMARK_ROOT=/home/rgardler/projects/llm python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark --sweep --resume 2 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>/n2_n3`
4. Copy that run's `slot_benchmark_report.json` / `slot_benchmark_summary.txt` to
   `.../n2_n3/report_2_3.{json,txt}` before the next invocation (overwrite protection).
5. If the N=3 run finished with `system_memory_bytes >= 40 GiB` (MemAvailable at run end,
   i.e. ≥ model+KV ≈ 27.4 GiB plus ~12 GiB margin) and no viability warnings, run N=4:
   `... python3 -m proxy.benchmarks.slot_benchmark --slots 4 --concurrency 3 --prompt-tokens 2000 --output-dir proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>/n4`
   Otherwise record a documented skip with the measured MemAvailable value.
6. Re-run the preflight gate, confirm `session_slot_pool_size` back at 2, `--parallel 2` on
   llama-server, `/health` ok, and `sha256sum proxy/config.yaml` equal to step 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Preflight JSON output (step 1) and the environment record (step 2) are committed in
   `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>/RESULTS_NOTE.md`, together with the
   exact commands and `sha256sum` of `proxy/config.yaml` before and after.
2. Committed results contain N=2 and N=3 runs (`slot_2.json`, `slot_3.json`, plus the
   preserved `report_2_3.json`), and an N=4 run (`slot_4.json`) or an explicit, quantified
   skip reason.
3. For every N run the results record: local TTFT (`dispatch_first_byte_ms`), decode tok/s,
   queue-timeout rate, denials, `finish_reason=length` count, requested vs observed
   llama-server `--parallel` (`observed_slots`), per-slot context clamp (`per_slot_ctx`),
   `system_memory_bytes` (MemAvailable), and local stream share.
4. Validity is explicit: each run's local stream share is reported; any run with share 0 or
   a viability warning is marked INVALID in both the note and the work-item comment, and no
   local-latency conclusion is drawn from it (matching the 2026-10-17/2026-10-20 precedent).
5. Config restoration is evidenced: post-run config sha256 equals pre-run sha256,
   `session_slot_pool_size: 2` restored, llama-server observed `--parallel 2`, proxy
   `/health` ok, and the preflight gate passes again at the end.
6. `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` in force is recorded with the results so queue-timeout
   rates are comparable with the 2026-10-17 sweep (60 s, not the 120 s assumed in the parent
   description).

**Key Files:**
- proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py
- proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_<YYYYMMDD>/RESULTS_NOTE.md
- proxy/config.yaml
- scripts/slot_sweep_preflight.py

## Notes / assumptions

- The 40 GiB N=4 gate is a documented conservative margin over the measured ≈27.4 GiB
  model+KV footprint; it is a threshold for the note, not a hard product requirement.
- Do not run this against the shared proxy during active multi-agent work (parent risk note).
  If the window cannot be made quiet, stop and report rather than run invalid measurements.
data.title: Execute N=2/N=3/N=4 slot sweep in a quiet window

# Fix the confirmed seed guard and document it

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a resumed session whose conversation actually continues
a persisted slot snapshot to earn the restored-prefix routing credit, while a
genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing — so the restored-prefix feature
(LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304) is measurable instead of silently dead.

## Why (evidence)

LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K found zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches in 54.4 h
despite healthy sidecar writing; LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E AC1 (via its diagnosis
child) names the confirmed failure mode from the instrumented
`slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts. This item applies the minimal change that
makes the common resume pattern earn credit while preserving the AC2/AC3
guards of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304.

## Scope

**In scope:** the confirmed-cause change to the seed guard (and/or the sidecar
TTL) in `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, evaluated at **both** call sites,
plus the red→green reproducer test and the `routing.md` update. **Out of
scope:** any change not needed for the confirmed cause, re-running the
measurement (sibling item), and any change to the sidecar schema version or
the fail-open behaviour.

## Proposed change

1. **Test-first:** write the unit test reproducing the confirmed pattern in
   `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — sidecar saved for a full
   conversation, resumed request arriving with a rebuilt system prompt or a
   front-compacted history (whatever the verdict named). Run it against the
   pre-fix code, capture the failing (red) output in a comment on this item,
   then make it pass with the fix.
2. Implement the smallest fix that credits the reusable prefix and still
   refuses a genuinely changed prompt, e.g. fingerprint the non-system
   messages only, anchor on a stable prompt-prefix hash, credit the
   last-saved overlapping messages, or compare against the last K stored
   fingerprints. Preserve the ratio cap (`min(1.0, cached/estimated) ×
   margin`), the sidecar schema version, and fail-open.
3. Evaluate the same guard change at the **second call site** —
   `provider.expected_cached_ratio()` (~L812) uses `prefix_matches` for the
   in-memory expected-reuse credit. Apply the change consistently there and
   assert a genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing (AC4 of the parent).
4. Re-evaluate the TTL only if the diagnosis proved it binding: either keep
   it, change the default in `ttl_seconds()`, or relax the check per the
   verdict's `age_s` evidence — with the number recorded in this item.
5. Update the restored-prefix warmness section of `proxy/docs/routing.md`
   (~L475–530): the resolved guard, what still earns nothing, the failure
   modes, and the config knobs that affect them.
6. Run the changed-scope test gate through the test skill; record the green
   result in a comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reproducer unit test matches the confirmed resume pattern, fails on the pre-fix code (red output captured in a comment), and passes after the fix.
- No regression on AC2/AC3 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304: a mismatched snapshot earns nothing and the restored ratio stays ≤ measured × safety margin — the existing cap and prefix tests (`TestRatioCap`, `test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match`, `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match`) stay green.
- A genuinely changed prompt still earns nothing: the existing `test_changed_system_prompt_does_not_match` and `test_front_truncated_history_does_not_match` expectations hold for the final guard, and the in-memory expected-reuse path (`provider.expected_cached_ratio()`) refuses the same diverged prompt.
- Sidecar schema version, sidecar format, fail-open behaviour, and seed success logging (`slot_ratio_restored`) are unchanged; no new config key is introduced unless the TTL change required one, in which case the default and its numerical justification are recorded here and in `routing.md`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` describes the resolved guard, what still earns nothing, and the failure modes, consistent with the parent's AC5.
- All changes land in the worktree of this item and pass the changed-scope test gate (build → test → commit order).

## Risks / notes

- The shared-guard note (parent intake notes): any `prefix_matches` change is
  a **two-call-site** change; the sidecar path test must be paired with the
  expected-reuse path assertion or the in-memory credit silently inherits a
  looser/different rule.
- Do not over-fit to the sample: the fix must generalise to a *reusable
  prefix* and still deny a *changed* prompt (AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304), not
  just make the observed session pass.
- The ≥24 h re-measurement that proves the fix belongs to the sibling
  re-measurement item; do not conflate this item's green test gate with field
  confirmation.

## Traceability

- child of: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (covers its AC2, AC4, AC5)
- blocked by: the diagnosis verdict (AC1 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E)
- implementation of: LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (restored slot-prefix warmness)
- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K

## Key Files (verified by inspection, 2026-10-22)

- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — the guard and TTL live here:
  `prefix_matches()` (~L159), `seed_cached_ratio()` validation order (~L349),
  `ttl_seconds()` / `_is_expired()`. Confirmed-cause fix lands here.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `expected_cached_ratio()` (~L812) reuses
  `prefix_matches` for the in-memory expected-reuse credit; the second call
  site that must change consistently (~L9084 is the sidecar seed call site).
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py` — add the
  resume-with-rewritten-front reproducer alongside the existing guard/TTL
  tests (`TestPrefixMatch`, `TestSeedCachedRatio`, `TestRatioCap`).
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — restored-prefix warmness section (~L475–530).

# Diagnose the seed failure mode from outcome counts

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the instrumented `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts
turned into a written verdict that names **the** failure mode behind zero
restored-prefix credits, so the fix on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E is chosen from data
instead of guesswork.

## Why (evidence)

LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K measured a 54.4 h post-deploy window with **0**
`slot_ratio_restored` seeds and **0** `cache_state=restored` dispatches, while
37 `slot_<session>.bin.ratio.json` sidecars were written and 33
sidecar-bearing sessions reached the local routing gate **2,918** times
(including immediately after proxy restarts, when the in-memory ratio was
empty). The producer therefore split the work: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 adds
INFO-level outcome logging (behaviour-neutral), and this item turns those
counts into the verdict the fix depends on.

The three candidate modes, in the order recorded at intake:

1. **prefix mismatch** — `prefix_matches()` rejects real resumed
   conversations (system prompt regenerated per request, and/or client-side
   compaction rewriting the front of the history);
2. **expired sidecar** — the 24 h `session_slot_ratio_ttl_seconds` is shorter
   than the save→resume interval of long-lived sessions;
3. **lookup miss** — the candidate snapshot/sidecar path resolves differently
   at seed time than at save time (recorded as unlikely: the directory names
   matched).

## Scope

**In scope:** analysis of proxy logs plus a written verdict on
LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit logic,
`prefix_matches`, the sidecar TTL, the sidecar format, or `cached_ratio`
scoring — the fix belongs to the sibling item.

## Proposed change

1. After LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 is deployed and has served at least one traffic
   cycle (target ≥24 h), aggregate the `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` lines from
   `/var/log/llama-proxy` using the aggregation recipe documented in
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`. Record the exact command and the per-outcome
   counts (including `found`) on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
2. For the dominant skip outcome, correlate the logged
   `stored_messages` / `incoming_messages` / `age_s` fields:
   - `prefix_mismatch` — compare the stored vs incoming message counts and
     identify *where* the fronts diverge (rebuilt system prompt versus
     front-compacted history); state how many of the sampled sessions show
     each pattern;
   - `expired` — tabulate the `age_s` distribution so a replacement TTL can be
     justified numerically;
   - `missing_snapshot` / `missing_sidecar` — confirm whether the session
     truly had no saved snapshot or whether the candidate lookup drifted, and
     record the candidate list if it is logged.
3. Write the verdict as a comment on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E: the confirmed mode,
   the count share that proves it, why the other two modes are ruled out (with
   their own counts), and which candidate fix it implies (fingerprint the
   non-system messages only / stable prompt-prefix anchor / credit the last
   saved overlapping messages / re-evaluate the TTL default).
4. If the counts are inconclusive (too little traffic, instrumentation gap, or
   a mode outside the three suspects), record that honestly, keep the fix item
   blocked, and file a follow-up item with the evidence instead of guessing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Per-outcome `slot_ratio_seed` counts over a window of at least one full traffic cycle (target ≥24 h) are recorded on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E together with the exact aggregation command used.
- A written verdict on this item (LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E) names the confirmed failure mode and cites the instrumented `slot_ratio_seed` outcome counts that prove it, with the count share; the two alternative modes are explicitly ruled out using their own counts.
- The verdict names the candidate fix it implies and explains why that fix still satisfies AC2 of LP-0MVGD9YXH008O304 (a genuinely changed prompt earns nothing).
- Where the confirmed mode is `expired`, the verdict includes the observed `age_s` distribution, so any TTL change is numerically justified.
- No change to the credit logic is made in this item: `git diff` over `proxy/proxy/` is empty for the credit paths (this is a verification-only item).
- If the counts are inconclusive, the item's closing comment says so, the fix item stays blocked, and a follow-up item is created with the evidence.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (2,918 gated decisions from 33 sessions in
  54 h); a single 24 h window may not sample every outcome. Extend the window
  rather than concluding from a handful of lines.
- The verdict must not be influenced by the unrelated local-prefill
  improvement recorded in the baseline report (attribution caveat on
  LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).
- If the instrumentation turns out to be missing lines for the common case,
  treat that as an instrumentation defect (follow-up item), not as evidence
  about the guard.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (measurement that found zero seeds)
- child of: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (covers its AC1)
- blocked by: LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7 (INFO `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…`
  instrumentation)
- blocks: the guard/TTL fix (its sibling) and the post-fix re-measurement

## Key Files (verified by inspection, 2026-10-22)

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — the outcome vocabulary and the documented
  aggregation recipe (added by LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7); the source of truth for
  how to count outcomes.
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — the existing measurement tool
  (windows, `cache_state` tables, sidecar inventory); reuse its window handling
  rather than hand-grepping where possible.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the
  zero-seed baseline this verdict is compared against.
- `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py` — read-only reference for the validation
  order (`snapshot → sidecar → model → TTL → prefix`) so each outcome maps to
  the branch that produced it.

# Re-measure restored vs cold over ≥24 h after the fix

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a ≥24 h post-fix window that proves the restored-prefix
credit actually fires (`cache_state=restored` dispatches exist) and that it
pays for itself (seeded dispatches beat cold dispatches in the same context
bucket), so AC3 of LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E is answered with real numbers.

## Why (evidence)

The baseline (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K) recorded **0** `cache_state=restored`
dispatches in 54.4 h and **0** `slot_ratio_restored` seeds — so the fix item's
green test gate is not enough; the field measurement is the acceptance test.
The pre-fix local-prefill improvement in that window was caused by other
changes (expected-reuse credit, admission ordering) and must not be used as
evidence for this path (attribution caveat on the parent item).

## Scope

**In scope:** deploying nothing new (the fix item's build), waiting out a
≥24 h window, and producing the before/after comparison with
`scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`. **Out of scope:** changing the seed
path again if the window shows zero restored dispatches — that reopens the
diagnosis with the new evidence rather than silently tweaking the guard.

## Proposed change

1. Confirm the fix build (the sibling item's worktree merge) is the deployed
   proxy version, and note the deploy timestamp.
2. Wait out a ≥24 h window (per shared background-job etiquette: launch, do
   other work, then one completion-aware wait). Optionally aggregate the
   `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts for the same window to cross-check the
   seed share.
3. Run `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` over the baseline window and
   the post-fix window (machine-readable `--json` output saved alongside the
   report).
4. State the verdict on LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E:
   - `cache_state=restored` dispatch count and `slot_ratio_restored` seed
     count (>0 required);
   - restored-vs-cold `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 with sample counts,
     same context bucket (reuse the bucket table layout from the baseline);
   - sidecar inventory at report time, and the `slot_save`/`slot_restore`
     confound rows.
5. Add the report (a section appended to
   `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` or a new
   file under `docs/dev/`) and link it from the parent item.
6. If the window still shows 0 restored dispatches, record the honest result,
   state the outcome counts that explain it (via the diagnosis item's
   aggregation recipe), and file a follow-up — do not claim success.

## Acceptance criteria

- A post-fix window of ≥24 h contains more than zero `cache_state=restored` dispatches and more than zero `slot_ratio_restored` seed events, with the exact counts stated.
- `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` percentiles (at least p50 and p90) for restored dispatches are stated against cold dispatches **in the same context bucket**, with sample counts for both groups.
- The same window's `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` counts are aggregated, so the restored share is explainable from the seeding outcomes.
- A written report is added under `docs/dev/` (or appended to the baseline report) with the command line used, and is linked from LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E.
- If restored dispatches are still zero, the verdict says so honestly, explains the outcome counts, and creates a follow-up item instead of claiming success.

## Risks / notes

- Snapshot-bearing traffic is thin (2,918 gated decisions / 54 h baseline);
  if a single day yields too few restored samples, extend the window and wait
  for a full traffic cycle rather than concluding early.
- The attribution caveat from the baseline applies in reverse too: a restored
  win must be attributed to the seeding path, not to unrelated local-prefill
  gains made in the same window.
- Schedule: this item cannot complete until the fix build has been deployed
  and exposed to ≥24 h of traffic — plan the wait, do not hold a slot during
  it.

## Traceability

- child of: LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E (covers its AC3)
- blocked by: the guard/TTL fix (its sibling)
- uses: `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`
  (LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K) and the instrumentation aggregate recipe
  (LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7)
- baseline compared against:
  `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md`

## Key Files (verified by inspection, 2026-10-22)

- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` — windows, `cache_state` tables,
  bucket pairs, sidecar inventory; run with `--json` and save the output.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-measurement-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.md` — the
  baseline tables and confounds this report extends.
- `docs/dev/slot-prefix-warmness-metrics-LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K.json` — the
  baseline machine-readable figures for side-by-side comparison.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy` — source logs (`.gz` aware tool), including the
  `slot_ratio_seed outcome=…` lines added by LP-0MVJYZWWW005XGW7.
data.title: Re-measure restored vs cold over >=24h after the fix

## Problem statement

Six `REFACTOR-<work-item-id>` provenance markers are still embedded in `proxy/` sources even though every referenced work item is **completed**. The refactor skill injects these markers when it files a smell (`remediate_pre_existing()` → `inject_refactor_comment()`) but nothing removes them when the item closes, so stale markers re-trigger refactor scans and re-file duplicate work items (LP-0MVIR51KL0096QOB was re-filed against an already-fixed F823 smell that LP-0MVJXC9MK003UET8 had resolved).

## Users

- **Maintainer running a refactor scan** — story: "As a maintainer, I want refactor scans to only report smells that still exist, so I do not triage duplicate work items."
- **Reviewer reading source** — story: "As a reviewer, I want the REFACTOR comments I see in source to point at open work, so provenance comments do not become permanent noise."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `REFACTOR-<id>` marker in `proxy/` whose work item is `completed`/`closed` is removed, together with any now-empty leading comment line — audited by a scripted check that greps `REFACTOR-` across the repo and asserts each remaining marker references a non-terminal work item.
- [ ] A regression test (or CI lint check) fails when a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker references a terminal work item, so stale markers cannot accumulate again.
- [ ] No behavioural change: `ruff check` and the existing suite stay green, and no non-marker source lines are modified (`git diff -U0` touches only comment lines).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Marker removal is a comment-only edit; do not change code behaviour or reformat the files.
- The refactor skill lives in `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` (outside this repo) — a cleanup step there must be raised as a skill-improvement item, not edited from this repo.
- Keep the diff reviewable: one marker block at a time, and confirm each marker's work item state with `wl show <id> --json` before removing it.

## Existing state

Markers currently present in `proxy/` (all reference completed items):

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` → `REFACTOR-LP-0MVIR51KL0096QOB`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` → `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` → `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA`, `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py` → `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z`
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py` → `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py` → (marker present; verify id)

## Desired change

Remove the stale marker blocks and add an automated guard (test or lint step) that rejects a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker pointing at a terminal work item.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — Remove the 4-line `REFACTOR-LP-0MVIR51KL0096QOB` block (lines 2-5)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — Remove the `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` block
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — Remove two stale marker blocks
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py` — Remove stale marker block
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py` — Remove stale marker block
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py` — Remove stale marker block
- `proxy/tests/test_refactor_marker_hygiene.py` — New regression test asserting every `REFACTOR-<id>` marker references a non-terminal work item

## Related work

- `discovered-from:LP-0MVIR51KL0096QOB` — the duplicate item that exposed the stale-marker loop.
- `LP-0MVJXC9MK003UET8`, `LP-0MVJXEWPJ002PG8H` — the completed fixes whose markers remain in source.
- `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` — another open refactor-generated item with the same worktree-path staleness pattern.
